sec01-card-sec01-F01.front: Where does a California driver's license legally allow you to drive?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.expected_back: A California driver's license lets you drive on public roads.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.front: Which two exams must you pass before California grants a driver's license, and where does their material come from?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.expected_back: Before California grants you a driver's license, you must pass both a knowledge test and a behind-the-wheel drive test drawn from this handbook.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.front: How many separate tests stand between an applicant and a California license, and what source covers both?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.expected_back: Licensing requires two different tests: a knowledge test plus a behind-the-wheel drive test, both drawn from the handbook.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.front: How must the license in your wallet correspond to whatever vehicle you take onto the road?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.expected_back: Your license must match the kind of vehicle you drive.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.front: Which specific license class covers everyday California drivers in standard passenger cars?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.expected_back: Most drivers need a noncommercial Class C driver's license.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.front: What changes on your license requirement if you switch to commercial rigs, motorcycles, or other specialized vehicles?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.expected_back: Driving commercial vehicles, motorcycles, or other vehicle types calls for a different license class.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.front: How does standard noncommercial Class C contrast with licensing for motorcycles, commercial trucks, and specialty vehicles?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.expected_back: Class C is the noncommercial license most drivers need, but commercial vehicles, motorcycles, and other types each need a different class.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: Which exact California DMV web address lists the vehicles covered by a Class C license?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: Details of which vehicles a Class C license covers are posted at dmv.ca.gov slash dl.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.front: Beginning in May two thousand twenty-five, what standard must your state license or ID meet to board domestic flights?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.expected_back: Starting in May two thousand twenty-five, a driver's license or ID card must be REAL ID compliant to board domestic flights.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.front: Which compliant California credential do you need when visiting or entering a military base?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.expected_back: A REAL ID is also needed to enter military bases.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.front: What credential standard do most secure federal buildings require before letting visitors inside?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.expected_back: Most federal facilities likewise require a REAL ID for entry.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.front: Which California DMV web path explains how to apply for a REAL ID?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.expected_back: You can learn about applying for a REAL ID at dmv.ca.gov slash realid.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.front: What three types of federally controlled access depend on holding a REAL ID?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.expected_back: REAL ID compliance unlocks three separate doors: boarding domestic flights, entering military bases, and entering most federal facilities.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: Which website provides official California details on registering as an organ and tissue donor?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: Information about becoming an organ and tissue donor is available at donateLIFEcalifornia.org.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: Where online can former service members check the rules and benefits for adding a Veteran designation?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: Requirements and benefits of a Veteran designation are explained at dmv.ca.gov slash veterans.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.front: How do the REAL ID mark, the Veteran designation, and organ donor status each serve distinct roles on your card?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.expected_back: Card designations split three ways: REAL ID governs federally controlled access, Veteran designation carries its own requirements and benefits, and organ donor status is recorded separately.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.front: How does immigration status affect whether a California resident can obtain a driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: California issues driver's licenses to every resident, no matter their immigration status.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: Who can get a California ID card, what is its sole purpose, and does it ever let you drive?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: Identification cards go to eligible people of any age for proving identity, and they never authorize driving.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: Which three items must an applicant bring when applying for a California identification card?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: An ID applicant must show an identity document, residency documents, and a social security number.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.front: Which DMV web address covers ID applications, document lists, and reduced-fee, no-fee, or senior ID options?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.expected_back: ID card applications, acceptable documents, and reduced-fee, no-fee, or senior ID card details are handled at dmv.ca.gov slash id-cards.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.front: What is the core legal difference between holding a California driver's license and holding a California ID card?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.expected_back: A license grants the privilege of driving on public roads, while an ID card only proves identity and never permits driving.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.front: What is the minimum age for a California ID card, and which three proofs are still mandatory?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.expected_back: ID cards are open to any age yet demand three proofs: an identity document, residency documents, and a social security number.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.front: How does California's immigration-status rule for licenses pair with the residency-document requirement for ID cards?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.expected_back: Immigration status never blocks a license, but ID cards still require residency documents among their proofs.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.front: How does California organize its online DMV pages across Class C coverage, REAL ID, veteran markings, and ID cards?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.expected_back: Each topic has its own portal: Class C coverage lives under the license pages, REAL ID under its own application pages, veterans under theirs, and ID cards under theirs.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.front: Which four specific visual tasks make up safe driving vision?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.expected_back: Driving vision means spotting hazards under changing light, judging gaps, matching traffic speed, and reading signs.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.front: Which four traffic sounds must drivers hear, and what headphone or earplug setup is illegal?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.expected_back: Drivers must hear horns, sirens, motorcycles, and screeching tires, and wearing a headset or earplugs in both ears is illegal.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.front: How do sight and hearing work together behind the wheel, and what ear rule keeps hearing open?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.expected_back: Eyes judge light, gaps, speed, and signs while ears track horns, sirens, bikes, and skids, and both ears must stay uncovered.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.front: What two critical abilities suffer when you drive tired or drowsy?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.expected_back: Fatigue and drowsiness degrade vision and slow reactions to hazards.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.front: What level of mental alertness should you maintain for unexpected traffic moments?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.expected_back: Stay alert enough to pick the right move fast in every traffic situation, surprises included.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.front: Can legal prescription or store-bought allergy and cold pills make driving unsafe, and what must you check first?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.expected_back: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can make a driver unsafe, sometimes through sleepiness, so learn every medication's effects.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.front: Starting at what patient age must California physicians report conditions like lapses of consciousness that could impair driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.expected_back: Physicians must report patients aged fourteen and up whose medical conditions, such as lapse of consciousness, could impair safe driving.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.front: How do drowsiness, legal medications, and mandatory physician reports each connect to driver fitness?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.expected_back: Tiredness dulls sense and speed, medications can sedate or impair, and doctors must report risky conditions from age fourteen.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.front: As your baseline habit, how many hands belong on the steering wheel?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.expected_back: Keep both hands on the wheel whenever possible.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.front: Which two clock pairs work for push-pull steering, and what rule keeps your hands clear of the wheel's center?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.expected_back: Hand-to-hand push-pull steering starts at nine and three o'clock or eight and four o'clock, never crosses hands past the wheel's center, and holds those spots through turns.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.front: How does push-pull steering maintain the two-hand default safely through normal turns?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.expected_back: Both hands stay planted by default, and push-pull keeps them at nine-three or eight-four without ever crossing center.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.front: In which three driving situations is hand-over-hand steering the right technique?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.expected_back: Hand-over-hand fits low-speed turns, parking, and skid recovery.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.front: Starting from which clock position, what step-by-step hand sequence executes hand-over-hand steering?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.expected_back: Its sequence runs: start at eight and four o'clock, reach across to the far side, release the other hand, then reach across the gripping arm and pull up.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.front: When reversing and looking backward, how many hands steer and where on the wheel does your hand sit?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.expected_back: One hand suffices when turning while backing to watch behind, with that hand at the twelve o'clock spot.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.front: Aside from reversing, what temporary task justifies steering with one hand?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.expected_back: One hand also suffices when working a control that forces a hand off the wheel.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.front: Which narrow situations allow crossing your arms versus dropping down to one-handed steering?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.expected_back: Cross arms only for slow turns, parking, and skid recovery, and drop to one hand only for backing at twelve or for forced control use.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.front: Which three built-in vehicle tools let you communicate with drivers, walkers, and cyclists?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.expected_back: Signals, horn, and headlights speak to fellow drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.front: Which four maneuvers require signaling, and what two conditions call for hand-and-arm signals?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.expected_back: Signal every turn, lane change, slowdown, and stop with lamps or hand-and-arm positions, using arm signals when lamps fail or harsh sun hides them.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.front: How may a bicyclist point out a turn instead of bending the left elbow upward?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.expected_back: Bicyclists may mark a turn by extending one arm straight toward that side.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.front: How do car signaling rules compare with a bicyclist's straight-arm turn option?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.expected_back: Drivers signal moves four ways with lamps or arms, and cyclists answer with one straight arm toward the turn.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.front: How far before a turn and how many seconds before a freeway lane change must you start signaling?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.expected_back: Signal at least one hundred feet before turns, ahead of every lane change, and at least five seconds before freeway lane changes.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.front: How should you handle signaling at curbs, on deserted-looking streets, and when turning right after an intersection?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.expected_back: Also signal curb pull-ins and pull-outs, empty-looking roads, and late-through-the-intersection turns coming right after it.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.front: What must you make sure happens to your turn signal right after completing a lane change or turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.expected_back: Switch the signal off once it has served its purpose.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.front: How do turn distances, freeway timing, curb and post-intersection rules, and canceling fit together?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.expected_back: Signal numbers pair up: one hundred feet for turns and five seconds for freeway lane changes, plus curbs, empty roads, and late intersection turns, then cancel.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.front: For what two safety purposes should you use your horn, including the exact sight-distance rule on narrow mountain roads?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.expected_back: Sound the horn to announce presence or flag danger: to avert collisions and to warn oncoming drivers on narrow mountain roads with under two hundred feet of sight.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.front: Within what distances must you dim high beams for oncoming versus followed cars, and may you drive using only parking lights?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.memory_hook: Five hundred oncoming, three hundred behind
sec05-card-sec05-F20.expected_back: Drop from high to low beams within five hundred feet of oncoming traffic and within three hundred feet behind a followed vehicle, since parking-lights-only driving is illegal.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.front: How do mountain horn warnings and high-beam dimming distances keep narrow or dark roads safe?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.expected_back: Horns warn of presence and danger on blind mountain bends, while high beams drop for oncoming and followed traffic by set distances.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.front: What visibility distance and exact sunset-to-sunrise window require turning your headlights on?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.expected_back: Light up when darkness hides beyond one thousand feet, from thirty minutes after sunset until thirty minutes before sunrise.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.front: Which five daytime or bad-weather conditions call for switching on your low-beam headlights?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.expected_back: Also light low beams for wiper weather, for murk such as clouds, dust, smoke, or fog, for mountain roads and tunnels even in sun, where signs command lights, and to stand out in low sun.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.front: What full set of time, visibility, weather, terrain, and sign conditions triggers headlight use?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.expected_back: Headlights answer darkness clocks and weather, murk, mountains, signs, and low sun together.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.front: Which three warnings alert drivers behind you when you spot a sudden roadway hazard ahead?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.expected_back: Warn followers of a hazard ahead with flashers, three or four light brake taps, and a hand signal while slowing and stopping.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.front: If your car develops mechanical trouble, what lights go on first and where should you steer?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.expected_back: Trouble stops start with flashers, or turn signals if flashers are missing, plus pulling fully off the road clear of traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.front: If your disabled car cannot clear the roadway completely, where must you stop and which two spots must you avoid?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.expected_back: When fully clear is impossible, stop where drivers behind can see car and driver, never just past a hill crest or curve.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.front: Once your disabled car is parked, how should you get help and where should you wait?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.expected_back: Call for roadside rescue and wait inside the vehicle until it comes.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.front: How do warning followers, parking a disabled vehicle, and waiting for roadside rescue connect?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.expected_back: Hazard ahead means warn behind three ways, trouble means clear the road and park visibly, and then wait inside for rescue.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.front: What must a vehicle hold before anyone can operate it legally in California?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.expected_back: Vehicles need California registration before lawful use in the state.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.front: Which specific California DMV web path hosts vehicle registration services and details?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.expected_back: Registration services and details live online at dmv.ca.gov slash vrservices.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: When you buy or acquire a vehicle in California, how many days do you have to transfer ownership into your name?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: Buyers hold ten days to transfer ownership into their own names.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: On what exact event does the buyer's ten-day ownership-transfer countdown begin?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: The ten-day buyer clock runs from the purchase date.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: Within how many days after selling or transferring a vehicle must the seller notify the DMV?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.expected_back: Sellers must notify DMV within five days of the sale.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: What is the official title of the form a seller submits to DMV after transferring a vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.expected_back: The seller's notice is the Notice of Transfer and Release of Liability.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: At which exact California DMV web address do sellers submit the Notice of Transfer and Release of Liability?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.expected_back: Sellers file the liability notice online at dmv.ca.gov slash nrl.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: How do California's lawful-use registration rule, buyer transfer window, and seller liability deadline fit together?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: Registration gates lawful in-state use with online services as the front door, while buyers race a ten-day transfer clock from purchase and sellers answer with a five-day liability notice filed online.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: How many days do new California residents or workers taking a job in the state get to register an out-of-state vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.expected_back: New residents and new California job holders hold twenty days to register out-of-state vehicles.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: Which two milestones start the twenty-day countdown to register an out-of-state vehicle in California?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.expected_back: The twenty-day clock starts at residency or California employment.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: Which California DMV web page explains all requirements for registering an out-of-state vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.expected_back: Out-of-state registration details live online at dmv.ca.gov slash outofstatevr.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: How does the out-of-state vehicle registration deadline compare with the seller and buyer clocks in this chapter?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.memory_hook: Five seller, ten buyer, twenty newcomer
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: Newcomers trade residency or employment for a twenty-day out-of-state registration window with its own service page, the longest clock in the section.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.front: What clean-air requirement must registered vehicles satisfy in California, and what does DMV do if a vehicle fails to qualify?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.expected_back: Registered vehicles must meet California emission controls supporting clean-air standards, and DMV refuses vehicles that do not qualify.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.front: How does California's emission-control requirement differ from the five-day, ten-day, and twenty-day filing clocks?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.expected_back: Emissions compliance gates registration itself with refusal as the penalty, standing apart from every deadline as a qualification rule.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.front: If you become concerned about your own driving habits, what two practical ways does DMV recommend to evaluate and improve them?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.memory_hook: Trusted licensed observer or pro lessons
sec12-card-sec12-F01.expected_back: Every driver eventually assesses personal driving skill; the concerned recruit a trusted licensed observer to note dangerous behaviors and suggest fixes, listen and apply the feedback, or take professional lessons instead.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.front: On which grounds can DMV reexamine a driver's ability to operate safely — and which factor can NEVER trigger reexamination by itself?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.memory_hook: Conditions or record, never age alone
sec12-card-sec12-F02.expected_back: The Vehicle Code lets DMV investigate and reexamine any driver's safe-operation ability on the basis of physical or mental conditions or poor records, never age alone.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.front: Which three groups commonly refer an unsafe driver for medical or mental review, and which exact DMV form do they submit?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.memory_hook: Doctors, police, family file DS six-ninety-nine
sec12-card-sec12-F03.expected_back: Physicians, law enforcement, and family members refer drivers with physical or mental conditions by submitting a completed Request for Driver Reexamination, form DS six hundred ninety-nine.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.front: Which neurological or cognitive conditions threaten safe driving, and what happens when someone is referred with mild cognitive impairment?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.memory_hook: Cognitive disorders trigger Driver Safety review
sec12-card-sec12-F04.expected_back: Cognitive disorders from dementia and seizures through brain tumors, Parkinson's, strokes, and vertigo threaten safe driving and can end it; mild-impairment referrals trigger Driver Safety reexaminations detailed at dmv.ca.gov slash reexamination.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.front: Across medical records, interviews, testing, license terms, and urgent hazards, what actions can DMV take during or after a reexamination?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.memory_hook: No action up to instant revocation
sec12-card-sec12-F05.expected_back: DMV reexaminations may request medical information, run in-person or telephone reviews, require knowledge, vision, or driving tests, issue limited-term licenses, immediately suspend or revoke privileges for immediate public threats, or take no action.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.front: How do voluntary skill checks, DS six hundred ninety-nine referrals, the never-age rule, and DMV's menu of outcomes connect?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.memory_hook: Observe early, refer conditions, tailor action
sec12-card-sec12-R01.expected_back: Self-evaluation pairs trusted-observer feedback against professional lessons, reexamination pairs condition-or-record triggers against never-age rules with physician, officer, and family referrals on form DS six hundred ninety-nine, cognitive disorders pair diagnosis lists against mandatory Driver Safety reviews, and DMV answers range from medical requests through tests and limited terms to instant suspension or nothing.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.front: If an officer hands you a Notice of Priority Reexamination with the top box checked, how soon must you contact DMV to avoid automatic suspension?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.memory_hook: Five working days or automatic suspension
sec12-card-sec12-F06.expected_back: Drivers handed a Notice of Priority Reexamination with the top box checked hold five working days to contact DMV and start the process before automatic suspension.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.front: What roadside situation leads an officer to issue a Priority Reexamination notice, and where do the copies go?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.expected_back: Priority notices rest on incapacity evidence at a Vehicle Code violation suggesting the driver cannot operate without danger; drivers receive copies while officers fax and mail the notice to the Driver Safety Office.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.front: Under California's priority reexamination sections, how long does a non-compliance suspension last if you miss the five-working-day contact window?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.memory_hook: Miss five days, suspended until passed
sec12-card-sec12-F08.expected_back: Non-compliance notices order DMV contact under Vehicle Code sections twelve thousand eight hundred eighteen and twelve thousand eight hundred nineteen, with missed five-working-day windows suspending driving until a satisfactory reexamination.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.front: Why does DMV place restrictions on a driver license, and whose findings determine what restrictions are reasonable and necessary?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.memory_hook: Examiner findings keep driving within ability
sec12-card-sec12-F09.expected_back: License restrictions keep drivers operating within their abilities, imposed by DMV or required by law, always reasonable and necessary, and always rooted in examiner findings and recommendations.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.front: What four categories of equipment, vision, or route limits can DMV add as restrictions on a license?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.expected_back: Restrictions may demand vehicle devices like hand controls, time-and-place limits like no night or freeway driving, eyeglasses or corrective contacts, or added equipment like outside mirrors.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.front: Are there special California license restrictions applied automatically to senior citizens?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.memory_hook: Restrictions answer conditions, never senior age
sec12-card-sec12-F11.expected_back: No restrictions target seniors specifically; every restriction answers a condition, never an age.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.front: How do the five-working-day priority notice rule and condition-based license restrictions work together to protect road safety?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.memory_hook: Contact in five, tailor to condition
sec12-card-sec12-R02.expected_back: Priority notices pair top-box checks against five-working-day contact clocks with automatic suspension as the miss penalty, incapacity evidence pairs violation context against danger judgments with officer paperwork duties, non-compliance pairs code sections against suspension-till-pass rules, and restrictions pair ability-matching against condition-only tailoring across devices, limits, glasses, and mirrors.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: If you do not already hold a California or out-of-state license, what must you get before booking a behind-the-wheel drive test?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: Without a license from California or another state, you must hold an instruction permit before you may take the behind-the-wheel drive test.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: Which foundational proof must accompany every California permit or driver's license application?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: A permit or license application must include proof of identity showing who you are.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: How many California residency documents are normally required with a permit or license application?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: You must also show two proofs that you live in California, though exceptions may apply.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: What extra paperwork is required when the name on your identity proof does not match the name on your application?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: When the name on your identity document differs from your application, you must add a legal full name document proving your current name.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.front: Which federal identification number is generally required on a California permit or license application?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.expected_back: A social security number is required as well, with exceptions possible.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: Where online are California's up-to-date REAL ID document rules and eligibility details maintained?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: Current REAL ID document rules and eligibility are posted at dmv.ca.gov slash realid.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: Which state official and website manage voter registration in California?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: Voter registration runs through the California Secretary of State at sos.ca.gov.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: How do identity proof, two residency proofs, a legal name document, and a social security number each serve a separate job?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back: Four proofs do four jobs: identity says who you are, two residency proofs say you live in California, the name document bridges mismatched names, and the social security number identifies the record.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: Which completed form kicks off the process of getting a California Class C instruction permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: A Class C permit starts with a completed Driver's License and ID Card Application.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: Right after submitting your completed permit form, what must you turn in and what kind of fee do you pay?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: Next you hand over your documents and pay a non-refundable application fee.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: After paperwork and fees clear, which two types of screening must you pass to earn your Class C permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: Then you must pass your knowledge test or tests plus a vision test.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.front: Where on the California DMV site is the complete instruction-permit checklist posted?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.expected_back: The full permit steps and requirements list lives at dmv.ca.gov slash instructionpermit.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: Why does an unlicensed applicant start with a permit, and what are its five ordered steps from start to finish?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back: The unlicensed start with a permit before any drive test, and that permit itself takes five ordered steps: application, documents, fee, knowledge tests, vision test.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.front: Within the permit checklist, which items are actual pass-or-fail screenings rather than administrative paperwork?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.expected_back: The permit demands two test passes, knowledge and vision, while documents and fees are paperwork rather than tests.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.front: What is the earliest age at which a California minor can qualify for an instruction permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.expected_back: Applicants under eighteen must be at least fifteen and a half years old for a permit.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.front: Which educational course must a minor complete to qualify for an instruction permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.expected_back: Those minors must also finish a driver education program.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.front: Who must sign a minor's permit application, what liability do they accept, and what changes under joint custody?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.expected_back: A parent or guardian must sign the minor's application, accepting financial responsibility, and both parents must sign under joint custody.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.front: Can a minor practice with family right after walking out of the DMV, or what must happen first?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.expected_back: The minor may not use the permit until behind-the-wheel training begins with an instructor who validates it.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.front: Where can teens take approved driver education and training, and what credential should you ask an instructor to show?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.expected_back: Driver education and training come from DMV-licensed driving schools and some high schools, whose instructors must carry an instructor ID card you should ask to see.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.front: Which California DMV web page offers tips on picking an approved driving school?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.expected_back: Guidance on choosing a driving school sits at dmv.ca.gov slash driver-ed.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.front: Who must ride with a permit holder during practice, how do age floors split for adults versus minors, and where must they sit?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.expected_back: Permit practice needs a California-licensed driver at least eighteen years old, or twenty-five for minors, sitting close enough to seize control.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: Why can a twenty-one-year-old California driver supervise an adult permit holder yet not a sixteen-year-old minor?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back: Practice supervisors split by age: eighteen-plus suffices for adults, but minors need a twenty-five-plus licensed driver.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.front: Once you hold your instruction permit and log practice, what test still stands before earning your driver's license?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.expected_back: After the permit, the license itself still requires passing a behind-the-wheel drive test.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.front: What is the minimum age for a California minor to upgrade from an instruction permit to a driver's license?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.expected_back: Minors must be at least sixteen years old to move from permit to license.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.front: How long must a minor hold a California or out-of-state permit before the drive test, unless what birthday arrives first?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.expected_back: They must also have held an instruction permit for at least six months, from California or another state, or else turn eighteen before booking the drive test.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.front: Which two separate course completions must a minor prove before getting a California license?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.expected_back: They must prove they finished both driver education and driver training.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.front: How does California distinguish between driver education and behind-the-wheel driver training for minors?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.expected_back: Driver education is the program minors must complete, while driver training is the in-car instruction whose instructor validates the permit.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.front: How many total and nighttime supervised practice hours must a minor log, and who qualifies to supervise them?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.expected_back: They must log at least fifty practice hours with a California-licensed driver aged twenty-five or more, including ten hours at night.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.front: What four core numbers define California's teen progression from permit age to license age, hold duration, and practice hours?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.expected_back: The teen ladder runs fifteen-and-a-half for the permit, sixteen for the license, a six-month permit hold, and fifty practice hours with ten at night.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.front: Which DMV web page gathers teen requirements, the Parent-Teen Driving Contract, and the DPE Score Sheet?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.expected_back: Teen steps, requirements, the Parent Teen Driving Contract, and the Driving Performance Evaluation (DPE) Score Sheet are collected at dmv.ca.gov slash teendriver.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.front: What special term is printed on a California driver's license issued to someone under eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.expected_back: Licenses issued before age eighteen carry the word provisional.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.front: During the first twelve months on a provisional license, which overnight hours are off-limits for solo teen driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.expected_back: A provisional driver may not drive between eleven p.m. and five a.m. during the first twelve months of licensure.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.front: Which passengers are off-limits during your first provisional year unless a parent, guardian, or licensed twenty-five-plus adult rides along?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.expected_back: Nor may they carry passengers under twenty unless a parent, guardian, or California-licensed driver at least twenty-five years old rides along.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.front: What employment and commercial vehicle restrictions bind every provisional license holder?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.expected_back: Provisional drivers may not drive for pay nor operate vehicles needing a commercial Class A, B, or C license.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.front: What three core bans restrict every provisional driver in California?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.expected_back: Three bans bind every provisional driver: no late-night driving, no young passengers without a qualified rider, and no paid or commercial driving.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.front: Who must sign a medical-need exception note for a provisional driver, and what two details must stay in the car?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.expected_back: A medical-need exception requires a physician-signed note in the car stating the condition and the expected recovery date.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.front: Which school officials are authorized to sign a provisional driving exception note for school-authorized activities?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.expected_back: School driving needs a note signed by the principal, dean, or designee.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.front: What signed documentation lets a provisional teen drive during restricted hours for a job?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.expected_back: Work driving needs an employer-signed note confirming the employment.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.front: Who signs the exception note for transporting an immediate family member, and which three facts must it state?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.memory_hook: Parent note names reason, relative, date
sec02-card-sec02-F32.expected_back: Driving an immediate family member needs a parent or guardian-signed note naming the reason, the member, and the end date.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.front: Which specific authority signs the written exception note for medical, school, work, and immediate-family needs?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.expected_back: For provisional-license exceptions, the required note is signed by a physician for medical need, a principal, dean or designee for school, the employer for work, or a parent or legal guardian for an immediate-family need.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.front: How can a parent or guardian revoke their minor teen's California driver's license at any time?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.expected_back: A parent or guardian can cancel a teen's license by filing a Request for Cancellation or Surrender of a Driver License or ID Card form.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.front: What word distinguishes an under-eighteen license, and who holds the legal power to cancel it via the surrender form?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.expected_back: The provisional word marks the teen license, and the same parents behind it can cancel it outright with the surrender form.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.front: Which DMV web address handles legal name changes plus physical-description or gender-identity updates?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.expected_back: Legal name changes and license updates such as physical description or gender identity are handled at dmv.ca.gov slash dlservices.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.front: Within how many days after moving must you report your new address to DMV?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.expected_back: Movers must tell DMV their new address within ten days.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.front: Through which two channels can you file an address change, and who stays responsible for keeping your mailing address current?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.expected_back: Address changes go in online at dmv.ca.gov slash addresschange or by mail, and keeping the mailing address current stays the driver's own responsibility.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.front: Does reporting a new address automatically send you a fresh plastic license, and how do you get one if wanted?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.expected_back: A new address never triggers an automatic new license, though a replacement can be requested for a fee.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.front: How do the reporting deadline and plastic card replacement work together after you move?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.expected_back: A move starts a ten-day report clock but buys no card, while the optional replacement card costs a fee.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.front: Is there any grace period to keep driving once your California license expires?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: Driving while the license is expired breaks the law.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.front: Where do you renew or replace a lost, stolen, or damaged license first, and what is the backup?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.expected_back: Lost, stolen, or damaged licenses are renewed or replaced through dmv.ca.gov slash dlservices, or at a DMV office when online renewal is unavailable.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.front: When can DMV require extra identity proof, and what happens if your license expires on the same date as your identity document?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.expected_back: DMV may demand extra identity proof before issuing, and a license sharing its expiry date with the identity document forces you to supply a valid identity document.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.front: Whose signature is required on a driver license application when the applicant is under eighteen?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.expected_back: Minor applicants need a parent or guardian signature on the application.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.front: What happens to your previous license once a replacement arrives, and what must you do if the old card turns up?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.expected_back: The old card dies the moment the replacement arrives, so destroy it if it turns up.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.front: How do personal-detail updates, ten-day move reports, and paid card replacements each work?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.expected_back: Use DMV license services for a legal name change or other license-detail update. Report a move within ten days so DMV can update the address on file; this does not automatically replace the license card, which you may request for a fee.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.front: How does DMV split tasks across license services, the address-change page, and local field offices?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.expected_back: Online routing splits three ways: license services for updates and reissues, the address page for moves, and the field office as fallback.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.front: What does California law forbid with an expired card versus a card replaced by a newer one?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: Expired cards forbid driving and superseded cards forbid keeping, so destroy the old one when the new one lands.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.front: Which two extra requirements can apply before DMV issues a card for matching-expiry documents or minor applicants?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.expected_back: Issuance can demand fresh identity proof when expiry dates collide, plus a parent or guardian signature for minors.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.front: Which category of California driver license is ineligible for an out-of-state extension?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.expected_back: Limited-term licenses are barred from that extension.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.front: How long and by what method can an eligible driver away from California extend their license, when must they ask, and who is excluded?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.expected_back: Stranded out of state, request a one-year extension by email before expiry, unless the license is limited-term.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: How does California DUI law treat prescription or pharmacy medicines compared with street drugs and alcohol, and how does age shift tolerance?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: California DUI law covers alcohol and every impairing drug alike, drawing no line between street drugs and doctor or pharmacy medicines, with alcohol tolerance falling as drivers age.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: Which alcohol, medication, or mixed-substance states make driving illegal in California, what habit prevents accidental dosing, and what does refusing testing cost?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: Driving is illegal after excessive alcohol in any form including cough syrup, after any impairing drug including prescriptions and over-the-counter pills, or after any impairing alcohol-drug mix; read every label, and know test refusal costs a year of driving.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: What license penalty hits a thirteen- to twenty-year-old convicted of riding a bicycle under the influence in California?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: Riders aged thirteen to twenty convicted of bicycling under the influence face a one-year suspension or licensing delay once eligible to drive.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: What are California's rules on drinking or using cannabis in a vehicle, where must open containers ride, and which passengers are exempt?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: Nobody may drink alcohol or use cannabis while driving or riding; carried containers stay sealed and unopened, open ones ride in trunks or non-passenger spots never glove boxes, with bus, taxi, camper, and motorhome passengers exempt.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: How do California's substance rules connect legal prescriptions, mixed doses, teen cycling convictions, and trunk-only open containers?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: DUI scope erases the legal-illegal drug line and the alcohol-medicine line with age lowering tolerance, illegal-after triggers triple across alcohol, drugs, and mixes with label reading and refusal penalties attached, teen bicycling draws driving sanctions, and container law pairs sealed-carry against trunk-only open storage with transit exemptions.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: What illegal BAC thresholds govern drivers twenty-one and up, under twenty-one, on DUI probation, or hauling commercially, and is a BAC number required to convict?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.memory_hook: Zero-eight adult, zero-one youth, zero-four pro
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: Illegal BAC starts at zero point zero eight percent for drivers over twenty-one, zero point zero one percent for drivers under twenty-one, zero point zero one percent at any age on DUI probation, and zero point zero four percent for commercial licenses and paid passenger hauling; below-limit driving can still be unsafe, and DUI convictions need no BAC reading at all.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: What three personal factors and forty-minute decay rate drive BAC estimate charts, and what pour sizes equal one standard drink?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: BAC tables estimate levels by drink count, gender, and weight with zero point zero one percent subtracted per forty drink-free minutes, one drink equaling one point five ounces of eighty-proof liquor, twelve ounces of five percent beer, or five ounces of twelve percent wine, fewer than five in one hundred exceeding the table, and even a single drink impairing.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: How does California treat alcohol and impairing drugs aboard boats, jet skis, water skis, and aquaplanes?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: Alcohol and drugs stay illegal aboard boats, jet skis, water skis, aquaplanes, and similar vessels under the Harbors and Navigation Code.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: How do California's tiered BAC limits, forty-minute decay charts, and watercraft sobriety rules fit together?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: BAC limits staircase by age, probation, and license class with impairment convictable below every line, table math pairs drink-gender-weight estimates against time-decay subtraction and standard-drink definitions, and vessels extend the ban offshore.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: Which chemical tests do California drivers consent to, why can't breath tests replace drug bloodwork, and what temp license and hearing window follow arrest?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: California drivers consent to breath, blood, or urine testing on DUI suspicion, PAS or breath tests never excusing drug bloodwork, refusal suspending or revoking driving, arrests triggering Admin Per Se suspension with seized licenses swapped for thirty-day temps, and hearings requestable within ten days of arrest.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: What license loss, classes, insurance proof, interlock, jail, financial hits, and record duration follow a California DUI conviction?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: DUI convictions suspend or revoke driving for a year plus a DUI program, SR twenty-two or SR 1P insurance proof, reissue fees, and possible ignition interlocks, with up to six months of jail, fines, impound and storage bills, and civil suits for injury or death on top, convictions haunting records for ten years with harsher repeats.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: How do California's implied-consent rules, immediate Admin Per Se arrest steps, and ten-year conviction penalties stack together?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: Implied consent stacks breath, blood, and urine with PAS never excusing drug screens and refusal ending driving, arrests pair Admin Per Se suspension against thirty-day temps and ten-day hearing windows, and convictions stack year-long loss, programs, insurance proof, fees, interlocks, jail, fines, impounds, suits, and decade-long records.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: When may a driver under twenty-one transport alcohol in California, how must containers be stored, and what job exception exists?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: Drivers under twenty-one carry no alcohol without a companion twenty-one or older, containers full sealed and unopened with opened ones in trunks or non-passenger spots, except workers for off-site liquor licensees with closed containers.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: What vehicle impound, fine, and license suspension or delay penalties hit an under-twenty-one driver caught carrying alcohol?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: For an under-twenty-one driver caught with alcohol in the vehicle, police can impound it for up to thirty days. The court may impose a fine and a one-year license suspension; for someone not yet licensed, it may request a first-license delay of up to one year.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: Which roadside tests apply to drivers under twenty-one, and what consequences trigger at zero point zero one versus zero point zero five percent BAC?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: For drivers younger than twenty-one, suspected drinking can lead an officer to require a handheld breath, PAS or other chemical test. A DUI conviction with a BAC of zero point zero one percent or more may cause a one-year DMV revocation, and a licensed DUI program is required. A PAS at zero point zero five percent or more may trigger a breath or blood test; a later result at that level may lead to DUI arrest and license suspension.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: How do California's under-twenty-one transport rules, thirty-day impound penalties, and zero-one versus zero-five BAC lines fit together?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.expected_back: Under-twenty-one possession pairs the adult-companion rule against sealed-container and trunk-storage geometry with a liquor-work exception, getting caught pairs impounds against fines, suspensions, and licensing delays, and consumption pairs test-on-suspicion against the zero-one revocation line and the zero-five arrest line.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: When must you carry proof of financial responsibility in California, and whom must you show it to after any collision?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: Carry proof of financial responsibility whenever driving and for drive tests, showing it to every driver involved after any collision.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: What three dollar minimums make up California's standard liability insurance coverage for injuries, death, and property damage?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: Minimum coverage runs thirty thousand for one death or injury, sixty thousand for multiple victims, and fifteen thousand for property damage.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: Who carries financial responsibility and pays crash damages for drivers under eighteen, and where can buyers verify insurance sellers?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: Parents and guardians bankroll drivers under eighteen and pay their crash damages while adults self-insure, and buyers verify agent, broker, and company licensing through the state insurance department.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: What suspension hits an uninsured driver after a collision regardless of fault, and how can you drive during the last three years?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: Uninsured crashers lose driving up to four years regardless of fault, win it back for the final three years by filing and holding SR twenty-two or SR one-P certificates, and the broke may qualify for the state low-cost auto program.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: Connect California's insurance proof rule, thirty-sixty-fifteen minimums, parental liability under eighteen, and four-year uninsured crash suspension?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: Proof rides along every trip and test with minimums staircasing thirty, sixty, fifteen across victims and property, minors borrowing parental coverage against adult self-coverage with licensed sellers only, and uninsured crashes trading four-year suspensions against certificate-backed comebacks and low-cost lifelines.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: What seven driver errors top California's crash list, and how should you drive past hazard flashers or a collision scene?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: Leading crash causes run distractions, unsafe speed, bad turns, ignored right-of-way, ignored signals and signs, wrong-side driving, and off-pace speed; flashers ahead mean slow careful passing, and rubbernecking only blocks rescuers.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: What is mandatory at every collision, when do you dial nine-one-one immediately, and when do you move cars off traffic lanes first?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: Every crash demands stopping since flight is hit-and-run with severe punishment, nine-one-one for the hurt, and moving clear before calling when nobody is hurt.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: Which four items must you exchange at a crash scene, and how fast must injury or fatal collisions be reported to police?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: Swap license, registration, insurance, and address with drivers, officers, and victims, and report injury or death crashes to law enforcement within twenty-four hours personally or through agents, brokers, or lawyers.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: What must you do if you strike a parked vehicle or unattended property versus injuring or killing an animal on the road?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: Struck parked cars and property need owner hunts or attached name-phone-address notes plus reports, while hurt or killed animals need humane-society or officer calls without moving them.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: Walk from top crash causes to immediate scene duties, document swaps, twenty-four-hour injury police reports, and parked-car or animal hits?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: Crash causes rank human errors from distraction through off-pace speed with flasher sightings and clear roads as responses, at-scene duties stack stopping against hit-and-run terror plus nine-one-one triage and document swaps, and twenty-four-hour police reports plus parked-property notes and animal calls close the scene.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: Within how many days — and at what dollar damage or injury threshold — must a collision be reported to DMV?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: DMV reports go out within ten days for crashes over one thousand dollars in property damage or any injury or death however minor.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: Who is responsible for filing the SR-one report with DMV within ten days, and do police reports, zero fault, or private parking lots excuse it?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: When a crash causes property damage above one thousand dollars, or any injury or death, an SR one report must reach DMV within ten days. The driver or a representative files it even when the driver was not at fault or the crash occurred on private property. Police do not file this report for the driver, and not reporting leads to suspension.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: How does fault affect whether a reportable thousand-dollar or injury crash appears on your California driving record?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: Reported thousand-dollar and injury crashes land on driver records by driver duty regardless of fault.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: Summarize the SR-one ten-day rule: dollar and injury triggers, private-property and no-fault scope, and driving-record impact?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.memory_hook: Ten days, thousand dollars, always recorded
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: DMV requires each driver to have an SR one report filed by the driver or a representative within ten days for a crash causing property damage over one thousand dollars, or injury or death. Fault and a private-property location do not remove that duty. DMV also records reportable collisions on the driver's record without regard to who caused them.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.front: Who has to take a DMV vision check, and what does it verify?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.expected_back: DMV vision-tests every applicant to confirm sight adequate for safe driving.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.front: What gets added to your driver license if you pass the vision check wearing glasses or contacts?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.expected_back: Testing while wearing corrective or contact lenses puts a corrective lenses restriction on the license.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.front: If you do not pass the DMV vision screening, whom do you visit and which form must they complete?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.expected_back: A failed vision test sends you to an eye doctor for a completed Report of Vision Examination (DL sixty-two) form.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.front: Which specific DMV web address publishes California's detailed eyesight standards?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.expected_back: Vision standards detail lives at dmv.ca.gov slash vision-standards.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.front: What question format makes up the required knowledge exam for a first-time California license?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.expected_back: An original license requires passing a knowledge test built from multiple choice questions.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.front: How many chances do you get to pass the knowledge exam under one application before starting over?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.expected_back: You get three attempts to pass before you must reapply.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.front: How long must an applicant under eighteen wait to retake a missed knowledge exam, and how is failure day counted?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.expected_back: Minors wait seven days, excluding the failure day, before retaking a failed knowledge test.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.front: Which drivers may choose the eLearning alternative, how is it structured, and on which devices does it run?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.expected_back: Renewals may substitute eLearning, a no-fail self-paced interactive modulated course with quizzes after each module, taken on computer, laptop, tablet, or mobile device.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.front: What step and web page unlock your California knowledge testing options?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.expected_back: Testing options open up once the application at dmv.ca.gov slash dl is complete.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.front: Which study materials or devices are permitted while taking your DMV knowledge exam?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.expected_back: No testing aids are allowed during knowledge tests, neither the handbook nor a cell phone.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.front: What question style, attempt cap, and minor waiting rule govern the DMV knowledge exam?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.expected_back: The knowledge test bundles format, attempts, and retakes: multiple choice questions, three tries before reapplying, and a seven-day minor wait excluding the failure day.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.front: When is the self-paced, no-fail eLearning module course available as a testing alternative?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.expected_back: During renewal, eLearning may be offered as a testing alternative: a self-paced interactive course with module quizzes and no failing result.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.front: Which two groups of drivers must or may have to complete a behind-the-wheel driving evaluation?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.expected_back: Original applicants take a behind-the-wheel test of safe driving ability, and renewing drivers with a vision or medical condition may have to take one too.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.front: Why might your DMV examiner give two or more directions together during the drive?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.expected_back: The examiner may stack two or more instructions at once to see whether you grasp and follow both.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.front: At what exact DMV web path do you schedule a behind-the-wheel appointment?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.expected_back: Drive-test appointments are booked at dmv.ca.gov slash make-an-appointment.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.front: How many days must a minor wait after missing a behind-the-wheel drive before trying again?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.expected_back: Minors wait fourteen days, excluding the failure day, before retaking a failed behind-the-wheel test.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.front: What distinct capability does each of California's three licensing evaluations measure?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.expected_back: Three tests gate three things: vision screens eyesight, knowledge probes rules, and the drive test grades real skill.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.front: What personal driving credential must you bring to your behind-the-wheel appointment if you hold one?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.expected_back: On test day bring the instruction permit or license if one exists.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.front: Who must accompany an unlicensed applicant to the drive appointment, and how does the age rule change for minors?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.expected_back: Also bring another California-licensed driver aged at least eighteen, twenty-five for minors, unless already licensed to drive.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.front: What condition must your drive-day car meet, and which two vehicle documents must be inside?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.expected_back: Bring a vehicle safe for the test plus valid insurance proof and vehicle registration.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.front: What two contract rules must a rental car satisfy before you can use it on your drive evaluation?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.expected_back: Rental cars qualify only with your name on the rental contract and no contract clause excluding drive tests.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.front: Which four requirement categories must line up on arrival for your behind-the-wheel appointment?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.expected_back: Test day needs four bring-categories: papers for you, a licensed adult beside you, a legal car beneath you, and rental terms that permit testing.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.front: What must be true of the driver's window and the windshield at the start of the pre-drive inspection?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.expected_back: The pre-drive check starts with an opening driver window and a windshield giving you and the examiner a full, clear, unblocked view, since cracks can postpone the test.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.front: How many rearview mirrors must your car have for the pre-drive check, and which location is mandatory?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.expected_back: At least two rearview mirrors are required, with one on the vehicle's left side.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.front: What brake light requirement does the examiner verify behind your car before starting?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.expected_back: Both right and left brake lights must work.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.front: What minimum uniform tread depth do tires need for the drive evaluation, and what spare type is prohibited?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.expected_back: Tires need at least one thirty-second-inch of uniformed tread depth, and donut tires are barred from the test.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.front: When pressed down, how much space must remain between the foot brake pedal and the floorboard?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.expected_back: The depressed foot brake must keep at least one inch of clearance above the floorboard.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.front: What three standards must your car's horn meet during the pre-drive check?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.expected_back: The horn must be vehicle-designed, working, and audible from at least two hundred feet away.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.front: Which four exact measurements govern mirrors, tire tread, brake pedal travel, and horn audibility on drive day?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.expected_back: The car's numbers cluster: at least two mirrors with one left, thirty-second-inch tread minimum, one inch of pedal clearance, and a horn heard at two hundred feet.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.front: What two actions with the parking brake must you show the examiner before pulling out?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.expected_back: You must show how to set and release the parking brake.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.front: Which three hand-and-arm signals will the examiner ask you to demonstrate through your open window?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.expected_back: You must demonstrate the left turn, right turn, and slowing-or-stopping arm signals.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.front: How are windshield wipers and seat belts handled during the pre-drive safety check?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.expected_back: Wipers may be function-checked, and every seat belt must work and be worn by each occupant.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.front: Which three hands-on demonstrations wrap up your pre-drive check inside the cabin?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.expected_back: The demo trio is hands, arms, and gear: set and release the parking brake, flash all three arm signals, and prove wipers plus belts.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.front: What happens to your driving evaluation if the car misses any pre-drive equipment requirement?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.expected_back: A vehicle that fails these requirements gets the drive test rescheduled.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.front: When is an interpreter allowed to assist you on drive day, and when must they step away?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.expected_back: Interpreters may help identify and use controls in the pre-drive inspection but cannot ride along for the test.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.front: Who rides inside the car during a behind-the-wheel evaluation, and what three exceptions exist?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.expected_back: Only the examiner accompanies the drive test, except for training, service animals, and certain law enforcement situations.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.front: How does DMV treat dashcams and other audio or video recorders during a behind-the-wheel evaluation?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.expected_back: Recording devices, including video recorders, are prohibited on the drive test, and one that cannot power off must be blocked from all visual and audio recording.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.front: How do passenger limits, interpreter rules, and recording bans shape the cabin once your drive begins?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.expected_back: Only the examiner rides along, interpreters stop at the pre-drive inspection, and every recorder stays off or blocked.

sec03-card-sec03-F32.front: Why does DMV prohibit automated parallel parking, lane departure helpers, and adaptive cruise control on drive day?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.expected_back: Because the test grades the driver rather than the car, assistance tech such as automated parallel parking, lane departure, and adaptive cruise control is banned.

sec03-card-sec03-F33.front: Are backup cameras and blind-spot monitors allowed on the drive evaluation, and what must you still perform?
sec03-card-sec03-F33.expected_back: Safety tech such as backup cameras and blind spot monitors is allowed yet never replaces direct mirror and blind-spot checks.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.front: What principle separates prohibited vehicle assistance features from permitted safety monitors during your drive?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.expected_back: Assistance tech that drives for you is banned, while safety tech that only shows you more is allowed yet never replaces your own eyes.

sec03-card-sec03-F34.front: Which two DMV web pages host sample Driving Performance Evaluation score sheets versus supplemental and area sheets?
sec03-card-sec03-F34.expected_back: Sample Driving Performance Evaluation Score Sheets live at dmv.ca.gov slash teendriver, with Supplemental and Area sheets at dmv.ca.gov slash seniors.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: What job do traffic lanes and road markings serve, and when does a single solid yellow center line forbid passing?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: Lanes carry single traffic lines, markings assign road space, and a lone solid yellow centers two-way roads and bars passing when bordering your single lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: Which four exceptions allow crossing one set of double solid yellow lines, and what do two sets spaced two or more feet apart mean?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: Never cross double solid yellows save HOV entrances, signed closures, lefts and U-turns over one set; twin sets two-plus feet apart bar all but gap crossings.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: When may you pass across a broken yellow line, and what kind of traffic does a single solid white line separate?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: Pass on broken yellow beside your lane when safe; single solid white divides same-direction lanes including one-ways.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.front: How do passing and turning rules step up from a single solid yellow line to one set of double yellows and twin sets two feet apart?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.expected_back: A lone solid yellow center line forbids passing only when your direction holds a single lane and that line sits on your side, whereas double solid yellow lines forbid every crossing except HOV entrances, signed detours, and left turns or U-turns over one set. Twin sets spaced two or more feet apart form a barrier no turn may cross except at openings.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: Where do double solid white lines appear on California roads, and when may you cross over into that lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: Double solid white walls off preferential lanes like HOV and rims ramps; never cross, and wait for broken white.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: What do standard broken white lines, wide oversized broken white lines, and painted white yield triangles each tell you?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: Broken white splits same-direction lanes; oversized broken lines warn of lane ends, heed exit and merge signs; yield triangles mark stop-or-yield points.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.front: How do double solid white lines differ in meaning from oversized broken white dashes and white yield triangles?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.memory_hook: Solid walls, dashes warn, triangles yield
sec06-card-sec06-R02.expected_back: Double solid white lines wall off preferential lanes and ramp edges and must never be crossed, while oversized broken white lines warn a lane is ending and yield triangles of white point at drivers who must stop or yield.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: Which side holds California's Number one lane, and which lanes handle passing or left turns versus entering and exiting?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: Lanes number outward from Number one; pass or turn left from the left, enter and exit from the right; far-left passing and reserved HOV lanes serve named users.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: What checks and speed habits make a lane change safe, and what must you do if you realize too late you are missing your turn?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: Signal lane changes, scan mirrors, sides, shoulder, blind spots, confirm room, hold speed; shun weaves, late moves, finish turns and crossings, loop back legally after a miss.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: How do numbered freeway lanes organize fast passing versus ramp traffic, and how do you handle a missed exit or turn?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.expected_back: Numbered lanes count outward from the fast Number one lane on the left, so passing and left turns belong left while entering and exiting belong right, and a missed turn means driving on to a legal turnaround rather than a last-second swerve.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: Which four vehicle groups qualify for HOV lanes during posted hours, what symbols mark them, and where may you enter?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: HOV lanes take qualifying carpools, buses, decal low-emission cars, motorcycles per posted counts and hours, show diamonds and Carpool Lane paint, open only at marked entries.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.front: How far may you travel in a center left-turn lane, and when must a slow vehicle on a two-lane road pull into a turnout?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.expected_back: Center turn lanes take turns only, at most two hundred feet, via signal-shoulder-merge; slow two-laners must duck into turnouts past five followers.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.front: How do access and distance rules compare across HOV lanes, center left-turn lanes, and two-lane road turnouts?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.memory_hook: Marked HOV, two-hundred turn, five-car pullout
sec06-card-sec06-R04.expected_back: HOV lanes admit only posted carpools, buses, decal low-emission vehicles, and motorcycles through marked entries, unlike the center left-turn lane which any driver may borrow for at most two hundred feet to turn, and slow two-lane traffic must yield at turnouts once five or more followers stack up.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: How are California bike lanes marked, and under what three situations may a driver legally enter one within two hundred feet?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.memory_hook: Enter bike lanes inside two hundred
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: Bike lanes belong to cyclists, show white lines, signs, green paint, and admit drivers only to park, enter or leave, or turn within two hundred feet.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: What six bikeway styles appear on California streets, and what blind-spot and clearance rules protect cyclists and motorized bikes?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.memory_hook: Check blind spots, give three feet
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: Six bikeways: plain, buffered, route, boulevard, separated track, shared sharrow; check blind spots first, ride motorized bikes gently, hold three feet from cyclists.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.front: How do the two-hundred-foot bike-lane rule and the three-foot passing rule work together around bicyclists?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.memory_hook: Two hundred turn, three feet pass
sec06-card-sec06-R05.expected_back: Bike lanes stay exclusive to cyclists apart from parking, entering, leaving, or turning within two hundred feet, and drivers must still scan blind spots, treat motorized bikes gently, and keep three feet from every rider.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: Where do you position your car to start a right turn, how far out do you signal, and what checks protect cyclists?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.memory_hook: Right edge, signal one hundred feet
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: Start right turns at the right edge or opening, borrow bike lanes only nearby, watch spots and curb users, signal near one hundred feet, check right, slow.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.front: What is a limit line, what three-step fallback tells you where to stop if none is painted, and where do you finish a right turn?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.expected_back: The limit line is the wide white stop bar; stop at it, else the crosswalk, else the intersection mouth; then left-right-left, turn safe, land right and tight.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.front: How does turning right on a solid red light differ from a red arrow, and what is the only legal move in a bus-only lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.expected_back: After a full stop, red permits a right unless a sign forbids it; a red arrow requires green. Bus lanes forbid driving, stopping, parking and leaving a vehicle, but may be crossed for a right turn.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.front: Walk through a California right turn: signal distance, three-place stopping priority, red-ball versus red-arrow rule, and bus-lane rule?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.memory_hook: Hundred signal, stop bar, arrow waits
sec06-card-sec06-R06.expected_back: Prepare a right turn near the road's right edge and signal about one hundred feet beforehand. Stop before the limit line, otherwise before the crosswalk, or otherwise before the intersection. A right turn after stopping at red is allowed unless a sign forbids it; a red arrow requires waiting for green. Cross a bus lane only to make the right turn, and do not drive, stop, park or leave a vehicle there.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.front: When a dedicated right-turn lane has its own signal or channel, what can you skip and what must you still obey and yield to?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.expected_back: Dedicated right-turn lanes skip merging and stopping, beat through-traffic reds, obey their own curb signals, still yield crosswalks.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.front: How far out do you enter a center lane and signal for a left turn, and why must your front wheels stay straight while waiting?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.expected_back: Lefts hug the divider or opening, join center lanes within two hundred feet, honor occupants, yield walkers, signal one hundred feet out, stop in order, swing to the left lane, hold wheels straight till committed, then accelerate.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.front: How do dedicated right-turn lanes with curb signals compare with setting up a safe left turn from the divider?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.memory_hook: Curb signals right, straight wheels left
sec06-card-sec06-R07.expected_back: Dedicated right-turn lanes skip the stop and beat through-traffic reds yet still obey their own curb signal and yield crosswalks, and left turns mirror the right-turn choreography from the divider with straight wheels until committed.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.front: Under what exact street combination is turning left on a red light legal in California?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.expected_back: Left on red works only one-way to one-way without a ban sign, yielding green traffic, walkers, and riders after looking both ways.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.front: What four road setups allow a signaled U-turn from the far-left lane in California?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.expected_back: Make U-turns with a signal from the left lane across double yellows, in residential two-hundred-foot gaps, at green lights lacking NO U-TURN signs, or through divided openings.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.front: At which eight locations — from railroad tracks and fire stations to business districts and one-way streets — are U-turns illegal?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.expected_back: Skip U-turns at posted signs, on crossings, over dividers and twin double yellows, under two-hundred-foot sight, on one-ways, at fire stations and driveways, in business blocks except intersections and openings.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.front: Pair California's one-way left-on-red rule with where U-turns are permitted versus forbidden?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.expected_back: Left on red is legal only from a one-way street onto a one-way street with no ban sign, and U-turns are allowed across double yellows, in residential gaps of two hundred feet, at green lights without posted bans, or through divided-highway openings, while everywhere else on the never list they stay banned.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.front: Which starting and ending lanes govern two-way lefts, standard rights, lefts from a two-way onto a multi-lane one-way, and one-way lefts?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.expected_back: Diagrams: two-way lefts center to center, rights hug the edge, two-way-to-one-way lefts start far-left, end anywhere past three lanes, one-way lefts start far-left, curb users and arrows govern.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.front: How do landing lanes compare across a two-way left turn, a single-lane right turn, and a left onto a three-plus-lane one-way street?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.memory_hook: Hug center, hug curb, open three-lane
sec06-card-sec06-R09.expected_back: Diagrammed two-way lefts hug the middle lane both entering and exiting, single-lane rights hug the right edge throughout, and a two-way-to-one-way left starting far left may finish in any open lane once three or more lanes run that way.
