sec06-card-sec06-F21.front: How do left and right turns work from a one-way onto a one-way, and who yields at a T-intersection?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.expected_back: One-way-to-one-way lefts start far-left with cyclist lane rights and open endings past three lanes; matching rights start far-right and end anywhere; T turns yield to through traffic, split from center.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.front: How should you transition off the gas to brake smoothly, and how much space do you leave behind a stopped car ahead?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.memory_hook: Coast, press gently, see rear tires
sec06-card-sec06-F22.expected_back: Brake by coasting off the gas, pressing lightly to a stop with room and time, holding behind limit lines, leaving rear-wheel sight gaps behind cars.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.front: Connect one-way-to-one-way corner starts, T-intersection right-of-way, and rear-wheel stopping space?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.memory_hook: Corner edges, T yields, tire gap
sec06-card-sec06-R10.expected_back: One-way-to-one-way lefts start far left with cyclists sharing the turn lane and finish anywhere past three lanes, matching rights start far right, T-intersection turns yield to through traffic from the center lane, and braking means coasting off the gas, pressing lightly, and stopping behind limit lines with rear-wheel sight gaps.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.front: Who yields when merging onto a freeway, what speed and following gap do you aim for, and how do you cross multiple lanes?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.expected_back: Merging yields: ramp lane at traffic speed, safe gaps sans stopping, signal, mirror, shoulder, three seconds, no solids, single-lane crosses with fresh checks.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.front: How many seconds — roughly four hundred feet — ahead should you signal in the exit lane before leaving a freeway?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.memory_hook: Signal five seconds, four hundred feet
sec06-card-sec06-F24.expected_back: Exits need foreknowledge, single signaled shoulder-checked moves, a five-second four-hundred-foot signal in the exit lane, safe speed, no solid crossings.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.front: How does the three-second freeway rule when merging contrast with the five-second rule when exiting?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.expected_back: Merging drivers yield to highway traffic by matching speed on the ramp, signaling, checking mirrors and shoulders, and holding three seconds of space without stopping or crossing solids, while exiting drivers signal five seconds ahead in the proper lane at a safe speed.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.front: How much clear distance do you need to enter city traffic versus highway traffic, and when should you hold off signaling right?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.memory_hook: Half block town, full block highway
sec06-card-sec06-F25.expected_back: Enter signaled with room: half a block near one hundred fifty feet in town, a full block near three hundred on highways; shun blocked intersections, fake right blinkers until turns truly start.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.front: How far ahead must hills or curves be clear to pass, and within what distance of intersections, bridges, tunnels, or tracks is passing banned?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.expected_back: Pass with room past oncoming users and hills, curves, and junctions a third of a mile out, scanning for drifters; never on blind hills or curves, within one hundred feet of intersections, bridges, tunnels, crossings, or hazards, at driveways, sans reentry room.

sec06-card-sec06-R12.front: Compare the city and highway entry gaps with the clear-sight and hundred-foot ban distances for passing?
sec06-card-sec06-R12.memory_hook: Blocks to enter, third-mile to pass
sec06-card-sec06-R12.expected_back: Entering traffic needs half a block near one hundred fifty feet in town and a full block near three hundred feet on highways, never into a blocked intersection, and passing needs a third of a mile of clear hill or curve while bans cover blind hills, junctions within one hundred feet, crossings, driveways, and missing reentry room.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.front: When is passing on the right legal, what shoulder move is always illegal, and what must you do while another car passes you?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.expected_back: Pass via signal, shoulder, lane, speed, signal-back; right-side passes fit multi-lane highways, left-turning leaders, one-ways, never off pavement or left of signalers; when passed, hold lane and speed.

sec06-card-sec06-R13.front: What five-step sequence completes a pass, which three setups allow right-side passing, and how does the passed driver behave?
sec06-card-sec06-R13.memory_hook: Signal out and back, hold steady
sec06-card-sec06-R13.expected_back: Passing runs signal, shoulder, lane, speed, signal back, right-side passes fit only multi-lane highways, left-turning leaders, and one-way streets, and a driver being passed must hold lane and speed.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.front: How much longer than your car should a parallel spot be, and what offset, angle, and curb distance finish the maneuver?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.memory_hook: Three extra, forty-five angle, eighteen curb
sec06-card-sec06-F28.expected_back: Parallel park with three extra feet: signal, pair two feet out, check spots, back forty-five degrees, straighten inside eighteen inches, settle parallel, brake, shut off, exit past traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R14.front: What four key numbers guide space length, pull-up gap, backing angle, and final curb distance when parallel parking?
sec06-card-sec06-R14.expected_back: Parallel parking wants a space three feet longer than the car, a roughly two-foot offset pull-up with the signal on, a roughly forty-five-degree back-in, and a finish parallel within eighteen inches of the curb with brake set and a careful exit.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.front: On the California drive test, how do you signal, check, and position your car when backing straight along a curb?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.memory_hook: Three car lengths within three feet
sec06-card-sec06-F29.expected_back: Back straight after traffic and blind checks, signal to the curb then cancel, mirror and shoulder-check, roll three vehicle lengths inside three feet watching behind, steer smooth, repeat to depart.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.front: Which way must your front wheels point when parked downhill, uphill with a curb, and on any hill with no curb?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.memory_hook: Uphill curb away, all others right
sec06-card-sec06-F30.expected_back: Hill parks set brake and park or gear; driveways aim out of the street, downhills bite the curb, uphills face center then kiss the curb rolling back, curbless slopes point right off-center.

sec06-card-sec06-R15.front: Pair the two threes of straight-line backing with the three front-wheel rules for parking on hills?
sec06-card-sec06-R15.expected_back: Straight-line backing signals to the curb, rolls three vehicle lengths within three feet of the curb, then cancels and repeats the checks to leave, while hill parking always sets the brake and gear with wheels biting the curb downhill, facing center uphill, and pointing right where no curb exists.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.front: What parking or stopping rules match white, green, yellow, red, and blue painted curbs in California?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.memory_hook: White brief, green timed, yellow load
sec06-card-sec06-F31.expected_back: White permits brief passenger pickup or drop-off; green limits parking by posted time. Yellow allows passenger and freight loading within posted times, usually with noncommercial drivers staying. Red bars stopping, standing and parking except buses at marked bus zones; blue needs a disability placard or plate.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.front: What clearance distances apply around curb ramps, fire hydrants or stations, and crosswalks — and where else is parking always illegal?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.memory_hook: Three ramp, fifteen hydrant, twenty crosswalk
sec06-card-sec06-F32.expected_back: Never park at NO PARKING signs, crosswalks, sidewalks, driveways, ramp three-foot zones, wheelchair curbs, disabled crosshatch, zero-emission bays, tunnels, bridges, hydrant and station fifteen-foot zones, crosswalk twenty-foot zones or fifteen at curb extensions, safety gaps, or doubled up.

sec06-card-sec06-R16.front: Review all five California curb colors: who may stop at red, who stays with the vehicle at yellow, and what unlocks blue?
sec06-card-sec06-R16.memory_hook: Red buses only, blue needs placard
sec06-card-sec06-R16.expected_back: At a white curb, stop briefly for passengers; at green, observe the signed or painted time limit. Yellow permits loading passengers or freight only for the posted time, usually with the noncommercial driver remaining present. Red excludes stops, standing and parking except buses in a designated bus zone; blue is reserved for authorized disability placards or plates.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.front: When is freeway or wrong-side parking legal, how long before a freeway car can be towed, and what habits save fuel?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.expected_back: Wrong-side and freeway parking need emergencies, officer orders, posted leave; freeway stops go fully off pavement behind locked doors under four hours; locals may reserve EV bays; drive green via smooth steady driving, kept tires, oil, filters, shed weight, per fueleconomy.gov.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.front: When an officer flashes lights behind you, how do you pull over, set up inside the cabin, and learn the reason for the stop?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.memory_hook: Right shoulder, window down, hands visible
sec06-card-sec06-F34.expected_back: At stops signal right, take the full shoulder even from HOV, find light, mute the radio, stay seated, drop the window, show hands, hear the reason before questioning save imminent peril, reasons logged on paper.

sec06-card-sec06-R17.front: How do freeway emergency parking rules and the opening moves of a law-enforcement traffic stop fit together?
sec06-card-sec06-R17.memory_hook: Off pavement, right shoulder, visible hands
sec06-card-sec06-R17.expected_back: Wrong-side and freeway parking survive only for emergencies, officer orders, or posted permission with freeway stops fully off the pavement and removable after more than four hours, and enforcement stops open with a right signal, a full move to the shoulder, radio off, seated waiting, window down, and hands visible.

sec06-card-sec06-F35.front: During a stop, how should you handle search requests, required driving papers, passenger ID, exit orders, and immigration questions?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.memory_hook: Show three papers, decline searches calmly
sec06-card-sec06-F35.expected_back: Decline searches aloud, never resist lawful ones; show license, insurance, registration or face limited searches; treat passenger ID as declinable-yet-sometimes-required, state refusals clearly, never meddle, obey seat orders; save immigration answers for federal officers.

sec06-card-sec06-R18.front: Which commands and documents are mandatory during a traffic stop, and which requests may you verbally decline?
sec06-card-sec06-R18.memory_hook: Obey seat orders, hand over papers
sec06-card-sec06-R18.expected_back: Drivers may verbally decline searches but must never resist lawful ones, must produce license, insurance, and registration, treat passenger ID as declinable yet sometimes required, obey seat and exit orders, and save immigration answers for federal officers only.

sec06-card-sec06-F36.front: When is recording officers in public protected, what if your phone is hidden in a pocket, and when does your phone stay locked?
sec06-card-sec06-F36.memory_hook: Announce before reaching, phones stay locked
sec06-card-sec06-F36.expected_back: Public recording is protected when announced and non-interfering, concealed reaches need permission, devices stay untouched, phones stay locked outside parole, retaliation is banned, rights gripes stay verbal.

sec06-card-sec06-F37.front: Where do you file a misconduct complaint after a traffic stop, and what anti-retaliation and anti-bias protections cover you?
sec06-card-sec06-F37.expected_back: Complain to the officer's agency for investigation, free from retaliation and bias across race, sex, color, ethnicity, national origin, age, religion, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, mental or physical disability, medical condition, citizenship status; contacts at post.ca.gov slash le-agencies.

sec06-card-sec06-R19.front: Summarize your California protections on recording officers, keeping phones locked, objecting verbally, and filing complaints?

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: How does braking recovery differ across four-wheel ABS, rear-only ABS, front-only ABS, non-ABS cars, a sinking brake pedal, and wet brakes?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: Locked skids follow hard fast braking; four-wheel ABS takes firm pressure, rear ABS eases to rolling then steers into the skid, front ABS releases and straightens, ABS-less cars pump, sunk pedals pump gently with downshifts and emergency brakes, wet brakes dry under gas plus brake.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: How much must you cut speed on wet roads, packed snow, and glare ice — and why is the very first rainfall so slick?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.memory_hook: Snow halve speed, ice max five
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: Wet roads cut five to ten miles per hour, packed snow halves speed, ice caps at five; shade hides ice that freezes first and dries last, bridges freeze first, and first rain on dry oily pavement demands instant slowing.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.front: How do your car's anti-lock setup and the road's surface layer together dictate pedal technique and speed?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.memory_hook: Match pedal to ABS, crawl ice
sec08-card-sec08-R05.expected_back: Locked skids answer ABS type with firm, eased, or released pedals against pump-and-downshift fallbacks, while slippery roads staircase down by surface: wet shaves miles, snow halves, ice crawls at five, with shade and bridges freezing first.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: When a heavy storm cuts visibility to around one hundred feet, what is your top legal speed and what gear must stay clear and ready?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: Storms cap sight near one hundred feet and speed at thirty; run wipers, low beams, and defroster, clear mud and snow off glass and lights, and carry correct chains in snow country.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: What warning sound hints at standing water, and what exact pedal rule saves you once your tires start hydroplaning?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.memory_hook: Hydroplaning: ease gas, skip the brakes
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: Hydroplaning floats the car on water with zero road contact, so slight inputs trigger spins; prevent with slow speeds, water dodging, slosh heeding, and gentle lane moves, and when floating ease off without touching brakes.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.front: How do you free a car stuck in deep snow or mud without digging the tires deeper or hurting someone?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.memory_hook: Low gear, straight wheels, gentle rock
sec08-card-sec08-F14.expected_back: Escape snow and mud with low gears and straight wheels, gentle unsprung gas, forward-reverse rocking to freedom, and boards or branches under the tires only while stopped.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.front: What links the hundred-foot storm speed cap, brake-free hydroplane recovery, and low-gear rocking out of mud or snow?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.memory_hook: Thirty in storms, ease hydroplanes, rock
sec08-card-sec08-R06.expected_back: Storm blindness pairs the hundred-foot sight line with the thirty cap plus wipers, lights, defroster, and chains, hydroplaning floats into brake-free easing, and snow burial answers rocking and traction aids.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.front: Which five hidden threats lurk in floodwater, when must you reroute, and what check comes right after driving through shallow water?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.memory_hook: Reroute deep water, test wet brakes
sec08-card-sec08-F15.expected_back: Floods threaten sweep-off, debris, collapse, breakdowns, and electrocution with unreadable depths; deep water means rerouting, forced crossings go slow, and brakes get tested right after.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.front: Which vehicles feel crosswinds worst, why should cruise control stay off in high winds, and what five steps keep you safe?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.memory_hook: Slow down, firm grip, kill cruise
sec08-card-sec08-F16.expected_back: High winds menace tall rigs most; slow down, grip firmly, watch for debris, shun cruise control, and pull over to wait out the worst.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.front: How do your post-crossing check in shallow water and your cruise-control rule in gusty winds keep control?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.memory_hook: Dry soaked brakes, skip windy cruise
sec08-card-sec08-R07.expected_back: Floods stack five distinct killers behind unreadable depths with rerouting beating slow crossings and post-water brake tests mandatory, while winds slow tall rigs into firm grips without cruise.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.front: If you cannot postpone driving in dense fog or wildfire smoke, which lights, listening habit, and pull-off rule apply?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.memory_hook: Low beams, crack window to listen
sec08-card-sec08-F17.expected_back: Fog and smoke favor postponement; forced trips go slow on low beams never parking lights, stop inside sight distance, widen gaps, wipe and defog, hold lanes, listen for hidden traffic, and pull off with flashers when too thick.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.front: When an officer weaves back and forth across freeway lanes with emergency lights flashing, how must drivers behind respond?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.memory_hook: Flash hazards, pace officer, never pass
sec08-card-sec08-F18.expected_back: Traffic breaks weave patrol lights to clear hazards, fog jams, and crash risks; drivers flash along, match the officer's gentle pace at distance, and never pass until lights die and conditions clear.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.front: How do hazard flashers work differently when escaping zero-visibility fog versus following a patrol traffic break?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.memory_hook: Pull off in fog, trail breaks
sec08-card-sec08-R08.expected_back: Fog forces low-beam patience inside sight distance with pull-off flashers as the escape, while traffic breaks convert patrol weaves into follower flashers, matched pacing, and no-passing discipline.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.front: At what age does a driver get ticketed for an unbelted passenger, and how fast does an unbuckled body fly in a crash?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.memory_hook: Buckle everyone, under sixteen on driver
sec08-card-sec08-F19.expected_back: Belts bind everyone with tickets for skippers and drivers answering for unbelted under-sixteens; crash physics keeps bodies flying at travel speed into glass and across seats, belts holding position and softening blows.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.front: Where must shoulder and lap straps sit on your body — including the exact belt routing during pregnancy?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.memory_hook: Chest snug, hips low, under belly
sec08-card-sec08-F20.expected_back: Belt right: shoulder strap snug across chest never under arms or behind backs, lap belt low on hips against submarining, pregnancy routing the lap low under the belly and the strap between breasts past the bulge.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.front: How do California's under-sixteen belt rule, human crash momentum, and low-hip strap placement connect?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.memory_hook: Driver liable, low hips stop submarining
sec08-card-sec08-R09.expected_back: Belt law binds riders and drivers alike with under-sixteen liability, crash physics explains the flying body and cross-seat sling, and correct wear routes straps across chest and low hips with pregnancy detours.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.front: What age, weight, and height numbers govern rear-facing infant seats, back-seat child restraints, and graduating to regular seat belts?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.memory_hook: Under two rear-facing, eight or four-nine
sec08-card-sec08-F21.expected_back: Kids ride approved restraints by size: under two, forty pounds, three-four height ride rear-facing never before airbags; under eight or four-nine ride restrained in back with narrow front exceptions; eight or four-nine graduates to standard belts, installs checked by pros.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.front: How do the three child-restraint stages step up from infancy to a standard vehicle belt, and who can verify installation?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.expected_back: Child restraints staircase by size: rear-facing infants with no front airbag exposure, back-seat boosters with six narrow front exceptions, then standard belts at eight or four-nine, with pro install checks.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.front: At least how many inches should your chest sit from the airbag cover, what if you cannot reach pedals there, and what side-airbag hazard affects kids?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.memory_hook: Sit ten inches from airbag cover
sec08-card-sec08-F22.expected_back: Airbags assist belts; drivers and passengers sit ten inches off the covers measured chest to wheel, dealers advising the cramped, and children beside side bags face grave risk.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.front: Under California law, what ages govern leaving a young child in a parked vehicle, and why don't cracked windows stop hot-car deaths?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.memory_hook: Six needs twelve-plus, never hot cars
sec08-card-sec08-F23.expected_back: Never leave six-and-under alone in cars with supervisors twelve-plus required, and never cook kids or animals in hot parked cars whose heat spikes even on cracked windows toward dehydration, heatstroke, and death.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.front: What does California's Basic Speed Law require even below the posted sign, and what default maximums govern multi-lane highways, two-lane roads, and towing?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.expected_back: The Basic Speed Law bans speeds unsafe for conditions regardless of signs, weighing traffic, surfaces, walkers, weather, and congestion without freeway weaving; defaults cap at sixty-five on highways, fifty-five on two-lane roads and while towing.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.front: Which key numbers govern airbag seating distance, child supervision in parked cars, and California's default highway speed caps?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.memory_hook: Ten inches, twelve supervises, sixty-five fifty-five
sec08-card-sec08-R11.expected_back: Airbags demand ten-inch standoffs for all seats with dealer help for the cramped, children stay out of hot cars and solo sits under twelve-plus supervision, and the Basic Speed Law caps judgment at sixty-five and fifty-five defaults.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.front: When a bicyclist rides ahead on your right at the same moment an oncoming car approaches, how do you separate the two hazards?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.memory_hook: Slow first, clear car, three-foot pass
sec08-card-sec08-F25.expected_back: Split dangers by severity: bike versus oncoming means slowing, yielding the lane to the car, then passing the bike with three feet or using the left lane against steady flows.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.front: When a tire suddenly blows out at speed, how should your hands, eyes, gas foot, and brake foot respond?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.memory_hook: Both hands firm, ease gas straight
sec08-card-sec08-F26.expected_back: Blowouts forbid panic braking or lifting; grip with both hands, hold speed while safe, ease off the gas, steer straight to stabilize, look where you want to go, then slow and pull off.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.front: If your right wheels drop onto a rough unpaved shoulder, how do you get back onto the road without crossing into oncoming traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.memory_hook: Ease gas, slow down, reenter gently
sec08-card-sec08-F27.expected_back: Pavement departures need a firm grip, foot off gas, gentle braking, a rear check, and a careful reentry, never violent yanks toward oncoming traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R12.front: What calm control principle ties together splitting dual road hazards, stabilizing a blowout, and reentering from a dropped shoulder?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.memory_hook: Steady grip, patient speed, smooth steering
sec08-card-sec08-R12.expected_back: Dual hazards resolve by severity with bikes getting three feet after oncoming clears, blowouts forbid panic inputs in favor of grip, hold, ease, and steer-straight, and pavement departures reenter gently without violent yanks.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.front: How do you protect an overheating engine on a blazing climb versus driving safely in freezing temperatures?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.memory_hook: Kill AC hot, check antifreeze cold
sec08-card-sec08-F28.expected_back: Heat waves demand gauge watching, no sustained speeding, and air conditioning off; cold snaps demand gauge watching for antifreeze gaps plus defrosting or cracked windows, manuals holding details.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.front: If your vehicle dies on a freeway, which side do you exit from, who do you dial, and when should you stay belted inside versus leave?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.memory_hook: Right doors, dial five-eleven, stay belted
sec08-card-sec08-F29.expected_back: Freeway failures pull fully right, exit and reenter from the right, call five-eleven or find a box, return quickly, stay belted inside with flashers as needed, abandoning the car only for missing shoulders, guardrails, or true refuges.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.front: During commute hours via five-eleven, which six free fixes can Freeway Service Patrol provide — and which four things will they decline?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.memory_hook: Free quick fixes, no private tows
sec08-card-sec08-F30.expected_back: Commute-hour freeway patrols give free gas gallons, jumps, radiator patches, flat changes, crash reports, and free tows to approved spots when dead, refusing private tows, shop tips, motorcycles, and crashes unless directed, all via five-eleven.

sec08-card-sec08-R13.front: How do temperature-gauge care, right-shoulder breakdowns, and five-eleven commute patrol rules fit together on California freeways?
sec08-card-sec08-R13.memory_hook: Watch gauges, stay belted, call five-eleven
sec08-card-sec08-R13.expected_back: Temperature extremes split gauge watching between speed-plus-AC discipline and antifreeze-plus-defrost care, freeway failures pull right with right-side exits, five-eleven calls, belted waiting, and rare abandonment, and patrols cover gas, jumps, patches, flats, reports, and tows minus privates, tips, bikes, and crashes.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.front: If your car stalls on railroad tracks with crossing lights flashing and a train approaching, which exact direction must everyone run after exiting?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.memory_hook: Exit fast, run diagonal toward train
sec08-card-sec08-F31.expected_back: Trapped on tracks facing a train with flashers: exit instantly, run diagonally away toward the train's origin side, then call emergency services.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.front: When your car gets stuck on tracks with no train in sight and no flashing lights, which number do you call first?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.memory_hook: No train: call posted crossing number
sec08-card-sec08-F32.expected_back: Trapped with no train or flashers: exit, call the posted crossing number with the crossing ID to report the car, then call emergency services.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.front: What cell-phone and messaging rules apply to adult drivers in California alongside everyday cabin distractions?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.memory_hook: Zero handheld phones, never text driving
sec08-card-sec08-F33.expected_back: Distraction kills through phones, navigation, kids, pets, music, and grooming; handheld use is illegal, adults go hands-free only when needed, calls wait for voicemail or pullouts, texts and emails wait always.

sec08-card-sec08-R14.front: How does the presence of an oncoming train change your track escape step, and what phone actions stay banned in motion?
sec08-card-sec08-R14.memory_hook: Diagonal for trains, posted sign quiet
sec08-card-sec08-R14.expected_back: Track entrapment splits on train presence: flashers mean instant exit with diagonal runs toward the train side plus emergency calls, silence means posted-number calls with crossing IDs first; distraction law bans handhelds with hands-free-only adults and zero-tolerance texts.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.front: Where and how may an adult touch a mounted phone, and what stricter wireless rule applies to drivers under eighteen?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.memory_hook: Single swipe mounted, minors emergencies only
sec08-card-sec08-F34.expected_back: Mount phones on glass, dash, or console clear of sight lines for single-swipe use only; minors face a total wireless ban behind the wheel except emergency calls.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.front: What should you anticipate when sharing lanes with driver-assistance systems or autonomous vehicles?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.memory_hook: Expect unusual moves from automated cars
sec08-card-sec08-F35.expected_back: Assistance systems and self-drivers react non-humanly, so expect alien responses to road events.

sec08-card-sec08-F36.front: Why can you never smell carbon monoxide leaking into a car, where must you never warm up an engine, and which six symptoms warn of exposure?
sec08-card-sec08-F36.memory_hook: Never garage-idle, six symptoms check exhaust
sec08-card-sec08-F36.expected_back: Carbon monoxide kills odorlessly from exhaust pipes, so never idle in closed garages; tiredness, yawning, dizziness, nausea, headaches, and ringing ears all demand an exhaust check.

sec08-card-sec08-R15.front: How do the under-eighteen wireless ban, autonomous-vehicle caution, and carbon-monoxide symptom checks round out safe driving?
sec08-card-sec08-R15.memory_hook: No teen wireless, watch sensors, ventilate
sec08-card-sec08-R15.expected_back: Phone rules pair mounted single-swipe use for adults against total minor bans except emergencies, assistance systems warn of alien reactions, and carbon monoxide pairs closed-garage bans with a six-symptom watchlist ending in exhaust checks.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.front: Which three core abilities must senior drivers maintain, and what realistic choice may eventually arise?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.memory_hook: Physical, visual, mental: limit when needed
sec13-card-sec13-F01.expected_back: Senior driving demands physical, visual, and mental ability, and the day may come to limit or stop driving temporarily or permanently.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.front: What three everyday warning signs indicate that a driver may no longer be safe behind the wheel?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.memory_hook: Lost nearby, fresh dents, close calls
sec13-card-sec13-F02.expected_back: Unsafe-driver warning signs run getting lost in familiar places, dents and scrapes on cars and property, and frequent close calls or collisions.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.front: What six practical adjustments can senior drivers adopt to lower risk while staying mobile?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.memory_hook: Daylight, light traffic, extra right mirror
sec13-card-sec13-F03.expected_back: Senior drivers may curb night driving with lit routes when necessary, favor light-traffic hours, dodge hard intersections, shorten trips to essentials, skip freeways, and add a right-side mirror.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.front: At which California DMV web address can drivers find the Driver Skills Self-Assessment Questionnaire?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.expected_back: The Driver Skills Self-Assessment Questionnaire lives at dmv.ca.gov slash driver-skills.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.front: How must drivers age seventy or older renew an expiring license, how early are notices mailed, and what option covers required knowledge testing?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.memory_hook: Seventy-plus renews in person, ninety-day notice
sec13-card-sec13-F05.expected_back: Drivers seventy or older at expiry renew in person with a vision test and possibly other exams, eligible for eLearning knowledge tests when required, with renewal notices mailed about ninety days out and missing notices answered by applications at dmv.ca.gov slash dlservices or offices plus samples at dmv.ca.gov slash driver-ed.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.front: Who does the DMV Community Liaison advocate for, and what one legal role can the liaison NEVER perform?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.memory_hook: Guides seniors and teens, never represents
sec13-card-sec13-F06.expected_back: The Community Liaison champions public safety for all Californians with senior and teen focus, mediating fair, lawful, dignified treatment, barred from hearing and reexamination representation yet rich in tools and information.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.front: How do warning signs, self-limiting habits, age-seventy in-person renewals, and the Community Liaison fit together?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.memory_hook: Spot signs, renew seventy, use liaison
sec13-card-sec13-R01.expected_back: Senior fitness pairs ability demands against limit-or-stop honesty with lostness, damage, and close calls as tripwires, coping pairs seven self-restrictions from night curbs to extra mirrors, self-assessment lives online, seventy-plus renewal pairs in-person vision against eLearning options and ninety-day notices, and the liaison pairs advocacy against no-representation limits.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.front: Which toll-free telephone number connects Californians to DMV Community Liaison and Outreach?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.expected_back: Area outreach and liaison contact runs through Community Liaison and Outreach at eight three three, four nine three, zero six seven five.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.front: What does progressive dementia eventually mean for driving, and which three groups must step in to stop unsafe driving and arrange rides?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.memory_hook: Dementia ends driving, three groups intervene
sec13-card-sec13-F08.expected_back: Progressive dementia ultimately ends safe driving, leaving caregivers, physicians, and law enforcement to halt seniors and arrange other transport, with reexamination details at dmv.ca.gov slash reexamination.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.front: At what starting age can Californians enroll in the Mature Driver Improvement Program, and how long is the initial course?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.expected_back: The Mature Driver Improvement Program runs eight hours for drivers fifty-five and older on topics of special mature-driver interest.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.front: What perk can Mature Driver graduates earn, how long does the completion certificate stay valid, and how short is the renewal refresher?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.expected_back: Insurers may discount program graduates on proof of completion certificates valid three years and renewable through four-hour refresher courses from DMV-approved providers listed at dmv.ca.gov slash seniors.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.front: Which two groups qualify for a no-fee California identification card?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.expected_back: Drivers sixty-two and older qualify for no-fee Senior ID cards, unsafe drivers of any age may trade licenses for no-fee ID cards good for identification only, and details live at dmv.ca.gov slash id-cards.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.front: How do the fifty-five mature course, sixty-two free Senior ID, any-age license exchange, and dementia intervention rules compare?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.memory_hook: Fifty-five course, sixty-two ID, dementia halts
sec13-card-sec13-R02.expected_back: Liaison contact centralizes on one phone line, dementia pairs inevitable driving loss against caregiver-physician-officer intervention, the mature program pairs eight-hour fifty-five-plus courses against insurer discounts with three-year certificates and four-hour renewals, and senior IDs pair sixty-two-plus no-fee eligibility against any-age unsafe-driver swaps for ID-only cards.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.question_text: Where does a California driver's license legally allow you to drive?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.teaching_text: Driving on city streets or highways without valid state authorization brings citations and vehicle impoundment.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.question_text: Which two exams must you pass before California grants a driver's license, and where does their material come from?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.teaching_text: Knowing traffic rules on screen comes first, followed by proving safe vehicle control in traffic.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.question_text: How many separate tests stand between an applicant and a California license, and what source covers both?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.teaching_text: Passing only the written portion earns practice eligibility, never full solo driving privileges.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.question_text: How must the license in your wallet correspond to whatever vehicle you take onto the road?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.teaching_text: Holding a standard passenger card does not make riding a motorcycle or rig legal.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.question_text: Which specific license class covers everyday California drivers in standard passenger cars?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.teaching_text: Everyday sedans, SUVs, and pickups fall under California's standard noncommercial passenger classification.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.question_text: What changes on your license requirement if you switch to commercial rigs, motorcycles, or other specialized vehicles?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.teaching_text: Two-wheel balance and heavy air-brake rigs require separate testing beyond basic passenger cars.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.question_text: How does standard noncommercial Class C contrast with licensing for motorcycles, commercial trucks, and specialty vehicles?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.teaching_text: Exam traps often test whether a regular Class C alone covers motorcycles or commercial haulers.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.question_text: Which exact California DMV web address lists the vehicles covered by a Class C license?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.teaching_text: Checking exact towing weights and passenger-van cutoffs online prevents accidental out-of-class violations.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.question_text: Beginning in May two thousand twenty-five, what standard must your state license or ID meet to board domestic flights?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.teaching_text: Showing a federal-limits state card alone at airport security blocks domestic boarding without backup identification.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.question_text: Which compliant California credential do you need when visiting or entering a military base?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.teaching_text: Base gate sentries enforce federal identification rules strictly before letting civilian visitors onto installations.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.question_text: What credential standard do most secure federal buildings require before letting visitors inside?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.teaching_text: Standard non-compliant state cards get turned away at guarded federal building checkpoints.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.question_text: Which California DMV web path explains how to apply for a REAL ID?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.teaching_text: Reviewing acceptable document checklists ahead of your appointment saves wasted trips to the counter.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.question_text: What three types of federally controlled access depend on holding a REAL ID?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.teaching_text: Everyday California driving works fine without one, yet all three federal checkpoints enforce compliance.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.question_text: Which website provides official California details on registering as an organ and tissue donor?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.teaching_text: Checking donor registry details before filling out your license form lets you decide confidently.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.question_text: Where online can former service members check the rules and benefits for adding a Veteran designation?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.teaching_text: Bringing the proper discharge verification paperwork upfront avoids having to rebook another counter visit.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.question_text: How do the REAL ID mark, the Veteran designation, and organ donor status each serve distinct roles on your card?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.teaching_text: Confusing optional card markings with driving privileges is a common first-time applicant mistake.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.question_text: How does immigration status affect whether a California resident can obtain a driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.teaching_text: Ensuring every resident tests on traffic laws and carries valid licensing keeps shared roads safer.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.question_text: Who can get a California ID card, what is its sole purpose, and does it ever let you drive?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.teaching_text: Handing an officer a state identification card behind the wheel still counts as unlicensed driving.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.question_text: Which three items must an applicant bring when applying for a California identification card?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.teaching_text: Missing even one required proof stalls your counter visit before your card can print.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.question_text: Which DMV web address covers ID applications, document lists, and reduced-fee, no-fee, or senior ID options?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.teaching_text: Checking fee-waiver and senior card rules online helps eligible Californians save unnecessary application costs.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.question_text: What is the core legal difference between holding a California driver's license and holding a California ID card?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.teaching_text: Both plastic cards look official in a wallet, yet only a license authorizes operating vehicles.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.question_text: What is the minimum age for a California ID card, and which three proofs are still mandatory?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.teaching_text: Children and seniors alike qualify at any age once they supply all three verification items.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.question_text: How does California's immigration-status rule for licenses pair with the residency-document requirement for ID cards?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.teaching_text: Applicants never face an immigration bar for licensing, yet proving you live in-state remains essential.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.question_text: How does California organize its online DMV pages across Class C coverage, REAL ID, veteran markings, and ID cards?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.teaching_text: Jumping straight to the matching subpage keeps you from mixing up ID checklists with license rules.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.question_text: Which four specific visual tasks make up safe driving vision?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.teaching_text: Safe eyesight goes beyond reading letters on an office chart to judging real-time speed and distance.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.question_text: Which four traffic sounds must drivers hear, and what headphone or earplug setup is illegal?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.teaching_text: Noise-blocking earbuds in both ears seal out emergency sirens and motorcycles hidden inside your blind zone.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.question_text: How do sight and hearing work together behind the wheel, and what ear rule keeps hearing open?

sec02-card-sec02-F31.teaching_text: Note that commuting to a regular job with an employer letter differs from banned driving-for-pay gigs.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.question_text: Who signs the exception note for transporting an immediate family member, and which three facts must it state?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.teaching_text: Vague family permission slips fail roadside checks if they omit who rides, why, or when.
sec02-card-sec02-F32.must_match_memory_hook: Parent note names reason, relative, date

visual_sync.text_span: Parent note names reason, relative, date

sec02-card-sec02-R08.question_text: Which specific authority signs the written exception note for medical, school, work, and immediate-family needs?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.teaching_text: Having a parent sign for school or work trips is a favorite DMV distractor trap.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.question_text: How can a parent or guardian revoke their minor teen's California driver's license at any time?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.teaching_text: Because parents carry financial liability for minor crashes, state law lets them withdraw consent anytime.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.question_text: What word distinguishes an under-eighteen license, and who holds the legal power to cancel it via the surrender form?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.teaching_text: Until age eighteen, teen driving stays conditional on both provisional rules and ongoing parental backing.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.question_text: Which DMV web address handles legal name changes plus physical-description or gender-identity updates?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.teaching_text: Knowing the exact license-services path keeps you from confusing personal record updates with simple residential moves.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.question_text: Within how many days after moving must you report your new address to DMV?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.teaching_text: Permit quizzes love swapping ten days with fourteen or thirty, so lock down the ten-day moving deadline.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.question_text: Through which two channels can you file an address change, and who stays responsible for keeping your mailing address current?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.teaching_text: Missing a renewal notice or citation mail because you forgot to update your file falls strictly on you.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.question_text: Does reporting a new address automatically send you a fresh plastic license, and how do you get one if wanted?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.teaching_text: Many drivers wait at the mailbox expecting a free reprinted card when DMV only updates its electronic record.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.question_text: How do the reporting deadline and plastic card replacement work together after you move?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.teaching_text: Separate the mandatory ten-day record update from paying extra only if you want updated plastic in your wallet.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.question_text: Is there any grace period to keep driving once your California license expires?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.teaching_text: Driving even one day past your expiration date is unlawful and exposes you to an unlicensed-driving citation.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.question_text: Where do you renew or replace a lost, stolen, or damaged license first, and what is the backup?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.teaching_text: Starting on the license-services portal saves an in-person line unless your account requires a field-office visit.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.question_text: When can DMV require extra identity proof, and what happens if your license expires on the same date as your identity document?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.teaching_text: If your legal-presence paperwork set your card's expiration date, renewing requires bringing updated valid proof.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.question_text: Whose signature is required on a driver license application when the applicant is under eighteen?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.teaching_text: Adults accept civil liability when signing for an under-eighteen driver, so DMV rejects unsigned minor forms.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.question_text: What happens to your previous license once a replacement arrives, and what must you do if the old card turns up?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.teaching_text: Carrying or using a canceled duplicate card after its replacement arrives creates instant trouble at a traffic stop.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.question_text: How do personal-detail updates, ten-day move reports, and paid card replacements each work?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.teaching_text: Keeping name updates, free address filings, and optional paid reprints clear stops easy mix-ups on DMV questions.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.question_text: How does DMV split tasks across license services, the address-change page, and local field offices?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.teaching_text: Picking the right portal first keeps simple moves and replacements off the field-office appointment calendar.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.question_text: What does California law forbid with an expired card versus a card replaced by a newer one?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.teaching_text: Once a card expires you park the car, and once a replacement lands you shred the old plastic.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.question_text: Which two extra requirements can apply before DMV issues a card for matching-expiry documents or minor applicants?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.teaching_text: Checking document expiration dates and bringing a parent co-signer prevents wasted trips for young or limited-term applicants.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.question_text: Which category of California driver license is ineligible for an out-of-state extension?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.teaching_text: Because limited-term expiration dates tie directly to federal legal-presence periods, DMV cannot extend them by email.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.question_text: How long and by what method can an eligible driver away from California extend their license, when must they ask, and who is excluded?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.teaching_text: Wait past your expiration date or hold a limited-term card and that one-year email lifeline disappears.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: How does California DUI law treat prescription or pharmacy medicines compared with street drugs and alcohol, and how does age shift tolerance?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Having a valid doctor's prescription offers zero defense in court if drowsy allergy or pain pills dull your steering reactions.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: Which alcohol, medication, or mixed-substance states make driving illegal in California, what habit prevents accidental dosing, and what does refusing testing cost?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Even night-time cold syrup or over-the-counter allergy tablets can stack with one drink and trigger a full year off the road.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: What license penalty hits a thirteen- to twenty-year-old convicted of riding a bicycle under the influence in California?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Teens assume lacking a car shields their future permit, yet a cycling conviction freezes driving eligibility for twelve months.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: What are California's rules on drinking or using cannabis in a vehicle, where must open containers ride, and which passengers are exempt?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Tucking an unsealed bottle or cannabis jar inside the glove compartment still counts as an illegal cabin container.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: How do California's substance rules connect legal prescriptions, mixed doses, teen cycling convictions, and trunk-only open containers?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Written exams bundle prescription pills, teen bicycle suspensions, and glove-box traps together to test every blind spot in DUI scope.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: What illegal BAC thresholds govern drivers twenty-one and up, under twenty-one, on DUI probation, or hauling commercially, and is a BAC number required to convict?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: Watch the below-limit exam trap: weaving or slurred reactions can still earn a DUI conviction even below posted thresholds.
sec09-card-sec09-F05.must_match_memory_hook: Zero-eight adult, zero-one youth, zero-four pro

visual_sync.text_span: Zero-eight adult, zero-one youth, zero-four pro

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: What three personal factors and forty-minute decay rate drive BAC estimate charts, and what pour sizes equal one standard drink?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Cold showers and strong coffee never speed up your liver, which clears roughly zero point zero one every forty drink-free minutes.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: How does California treat alcohol and impairing drugs aboard boats, jet skis, water skis, and aquaplanes?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Sun glare, wave bounce, and propeller hazards make impaired boating or jet-skiing illegal under state navigation rules.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: How do California's tiered BAC limits, forty-minute decay charts, and watercraft sobriety rules fit together?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Whether on pavement or open water, chart estimates cannot guarantee legality because impairment starts with the very first drink.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: Which chemical tests do California drivers consent to, why can't breath tests replace drug bloodwork, and what temp license and hearing window follow arrest?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Breathalyzers measure alcohol rather than pills or cannabis, so officers can still require a blood draw after a clean breath check.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: What license loss, classes, insurance proof, interlock, jail, financial hits, and record duration follow a California DUI conviction?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Beyond courtroom fines and up to six months in jail, a conviction stays on your driving record for a full decade.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: How do California's implied-consent rules, immediate Admin Per Se arrest steps, and ten-year conviction penalties stack together?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Losing your plastic card roadside for a thirty-day pink slip happens immediately upon arrest, weeks before any criminal trial finishes.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: When may a driver under twenty-one transport alcohol in California, how must containers be stored, and what job exception exists?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Even an unopened six-pack triggers a youth possession violation unless a qualifying adult rides along or off-site work duties apply.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: What vehicle impound, fine, and license suspension or delay penalties hit an under-twenty-one driver caught carrying alcohol?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: Getting caught transporting beer to a party can lock up the family car for a month and cost a year of driving.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: Which roadside tests apply to drivers under twenty-one, and what consequences trigger at zero point zero one versus zero point zero five percent BAC?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Permit exams contrast those two youth thresholds: zero point zero one revokes for a year, while zero point zero five escalates to arrest.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: How do California's under-twenty-one transport rules, thirty-day impound penalties, and zero-one versus zero-five BAC lines fit together?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Zero-tolerance laws stack container possession bans right alongside trace-level breath tests so minors face suspension even without drinking.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: When must you carry proof of financial responsibility in California, and whom must you show it to after any collision?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Showing up at DMV for your behind-the-wheel test without valid insurance proof gets your road exam canceled at check-in.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: What three dollar minimums make up California's standard liability insurance coverage for injuries, death, and property damage?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Watch the exact sequence on exam questions: single victim injury or death first, total victims second, and property damage third.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: Who carries financial responsibility and pays crash damages for drivers under eighteen, and where can buyers verify insurance sellers?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Until your eighteenth birthday, parents or guardians who signed for your license stay financially on the hook for crashes.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: What suspension hits an uninsured driver after a collision regardless of fault, and how can you drive during the last three years?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Even getting rear-ended at a stoplight suspends an uninsured driver for up to four years without fault protection.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: Connect California's insurance proof rule, thirty-sixty-fifteen minimums, parental liability under eighteen, and four-year uninsured crash suspension?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Locking down valid coverage before turning the key protects both your license and your family's finances after any wreck.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: What seven driver errors top California's crash list, and how should you drive past hazard flashers or a collision scene?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Slowing down just to stare at a roadside wreck clogs lanes for ambulances and sparks secondary rear-end collisions.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: What is mandatory at every collision, when do you dial nine-one-one immediately, and when do you move cars off traffic lanes first?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: Driving off from even a minor fender-bender turns an ordinary traffic mishap into a criminal hit-and-run charge.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: Which four items must you exchange at a crash scene, and how fast must injury or fatal collisions be reported to police?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Injury or fatal crashes need a written report to CHP or local police within twenty-four hours if officers did not respond.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: What must you do if you strike a parked vehicle or unattended property versus injuring or killing an animal on the road?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: Trying to lift an injured animal in traffic risks bites or getting struck; call police or humane responders instead.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: Walk from top crash causes to immediate scene duties, document swaps, twenty-four-hour injury police reports, and parked-car or animal hits?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Handling the scene step by step prevents hit-and-run charges, clears traffic safely, and keeps emergency responders moving.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: Within how many days — and at what dollar damage or injury threshold — must a collision be reported to DMV?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Even a slight whiplash ache or soreness triggers the ten-day clock regardless of how small the bumper dent looks.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: Who is responsible for filing the SR-one report with DMV within ten days, and do police reports, zero fault, or private parking lots excuse it?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Assuming the responding officer's crash report covers DMV is a classic license-suspending mistake; your side must file SR-one.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: How does fault affect whether a reportable thousand-dollar or injury crash appears on your California driving record?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: Every collision crossing the thousand-dollar or injury line enters your DMV record even when the other driver caused it.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.question_text: Summarize the SR-one ten-day rule: dollar and injury triggers, private-property and no-fault scope, and driving-record impact?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.teaching_text: Keep twenty-four-hour police injury reports separate from the ten-day SR-one DMV filing required on thousand-dollar or injury wrecks.
sec10-card-sec10-R03.must_match_memory_hook: Ten days, thousand dollars, always recorded

visual_sync.text_span: Ten days, thousand dollars, always recorded

sec03-card-sec03-F01.question_text: Who has to take a DMV vision check, and what does it verify?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.teaching_text: Spotting lane hazards and signs starts with clear eyesight, so nobody skips the counter screening.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.question_text: What gets added to your driver license if you pass the vision check wearing glasses or contacts?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.teaching_text: Driving bare-eyed after passing in glasses breaks your license restriction and invites a citation.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.question_text: If you do not pass the DMV vision screening, whom do you visit and which form must they complete?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.teaching_text: Memorize form number sixty-two because DMV quizzes love testing exact paperwork names for vision referrals.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.question_text: Which specific DMV web address publishes California's detailed eyesight standards?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.teaching_text: Knowing the exact slug after the slash separates the eyesight standards page from general licensing pages.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.question_text: What question format makes up the required knowledge exam for a first-time California license?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.teaching_text: Every first-time applicant faces multiple-choice items covering road laws and safe habits before earning driving privileges.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.question_text: How many chances do you get to pass the knowledge exam under one application before starting over?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.teaching_text: Missing a third attempt wipes your current application and forces a fresh filing and fee.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.question_text: How long must an applicant under eighteen wait to retake a missed knowledge exam, and how is failure day counted?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.teaching_text: Counting the miss day itself is a classic trap that sends minors back one day too early.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.question_text: Which drivers may choose the eLearning alternative, how is it structured, and on which devices does it run?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.teaching_text: Watch out because first-time permit seekers cannot pick eLearning since it applies strictly to eligible renewals.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.question_text: What step and web page unlock your California knowledge testing options?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.teaching_text: Showing up without submitting your online driver license form stalls your visit before testing even opens.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.question_text: Which study materials or devices are permitted while taking your DMV knowledge exam?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.teaching_text: Pulling out a phone or open handbook mid-session disqualifies your attempt on the spot.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.question_text: What question style, attempt cap, and minor waiting rule govern the DMV knowledge exam?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.teaching_text: Keep seven days for written retakes separate from the longer two-week wait on road retakes.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.question_text: When is the self-paced, no-fail eLearning module course available as a testing alternative?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.teaching_text: Interactive module quizzes check comprehension along the way without threatening renewing drivers with a failing grade.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.question_text: Which two groups of drivers must or may have to complete a behind-the-wheel driving evaluation?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.teaching_text: Even experienced renewing drivers can be called onto the road course if eyesight or health changes raise safety questions.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.question_text: Why might your DMV examiner give two or more directions together during the drive?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.teaching_text: Everyday traffic demands planning a lane change and an upcoming turn together without losing focus.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.question_text: At what exact DMV web path do you schedule a behind-the-wheel appointment?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.teaching_text: Walk-in behind-the-wheel slots do not exist, so booking through the appointment portal is mandatory.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.question_text: How many days must a minor wait after missing a behind-the-wheel drive before trying again?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.teaching_text: Notice the road retake wait doubles the seven-day written wait, and neither count includes failure day.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.question_text: What distinct capability does each of California's three licensing evaluations measure?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.teaching_text: Passing all three stages proves you can spot hazards clearly, recall road law, and handle traffic smoothly.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.question_text: What personal driving credential must you bring to your behind-the-wheel appointment if you hold one?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.teaching_text: Leaving your instruction permit at home stops check-in cold before the examiner ever walks outside.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.question_text: Who must accompany an unlicensed applicant to the drive appointment, and how does the age rule change for minors?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.teaching_text: Teens often bring an eighteen-year-old sibling by mistake when California strictly requires twenty-five or older for minors.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.question_text: What condition must your drive-day car meet, and which two vehicle documents must be inside?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.teaching_text: Expired registration or missing insurance proof cancels your appointment right in the inspection lane.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.question_text: What two contract rules must a rental car satisfy before you can use it on your drive evaluation?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.teaching_text: Most rental agreements bar learner evaluations or omit teen names, disqualifying the car at check-in.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.question_text: Which four requirement categories must line up on arrival for your behind-the-wheel appointment?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.teaching_text: Double-checking your permit, accompanying driver's age, car papers, and any rental contract saves wasted months rebooking.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.question_text: What must be true of the driver's window and the windshield at the start of the pre-drive inspection?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.teaching_text: You need an open driver window for hand signals while spiderweb glass blocks the examiner's sightline.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.question_text: How many rearview mirrors must your car have for the pre-drive check, and which location is mandatory?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.teaching_text: Missing that outside left mirror fails the pre-drive inspection immediately even if center and right mirrors remain.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.question_text: What brake light requirement does the examiner verify behind your car before starting?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.teaching_text: A single burned-out tail bulb postpones your drive evaluation, so have someone check your brake pedal glow beforehand.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.question_text: What minimum uniform tread depth do tires need for the drive evaluation, and what spare type is prohibited?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.teaching_text: Temporary compact spares lack full braking grip and stability, earning an automatic reschedule in the inspection lane.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.question_text: When pressed down, how much space must remain between the foot brake pedal and the floorboard?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.teaching_text: A spongy pedal sinking near the carpet signals weak hydraulic pressure that could fail during a hard stop.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.question_text: What three standards must your car's horn meet during the pre-drive check?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.teaching_text: Novelty air horns or weak chimes fail inspection because emergency warnings must carry two hundred feet down traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.question_text: Which four exact measurements govern mirrors, tire tread, brake pedal travel, and horn audibility on drive day?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.teaching_text: Quiz writers swap one-inch pedal space with tire tread fractions, so anchor each measurement to its part.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.question_text: What two actions with the parking brake must you show the examiner before pulling out?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.teaching_text: Fumbling for an unfamiliar foot pedal or electronic switch adds nerves, so practice engaging and releasing yours first.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.question_text: Which three hand-and-arm signals will the examiner ask you to demonstrate through your open window?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.teaching_text: Mixing up upward right-turn and downward stop positions costs easy pre-drive points before the wheels even roll.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.question_text: How are windshield wipers and seat belts handled during the pre-drive safety check?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.teaching_text: Even on a sunny California afternoon, you may have to switch wipers on while both occupants stay buckled.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.question_text: Which three hands-on demonstrations wrap up your pre-drive check inside the cabin?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.teaching_text: Running through every cabin control in a borrowed parent car the night before keeps your start calm.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.question_text: What happens to your driving evaluation if the car misses any pre-drive equipment requirement?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.teaching_text: A burned-out bulb or cracked windshield will not count as a driving failure, yet it still costs your appointment.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.question_text: When is an interpreter allowed to assist you on drive day, and when must they step away?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.teaching_text: Once the vehicle rolls onto public streets, you must understand spoken traffic directions directly without translation.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.question_text: Who rides inside the car during a behind-the-wheel evaluation, and what three exceptions exist?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.teaching_text: Parents, friends, and instructors wait back at the office while only authorized staff, service animals, or officers ride.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.question_text: How does DMV treat dashcams and other audio or video recorders during a behind-the-wheel evaluation?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.teaching_text: Built-in cabin or dash cameras that stay wired on must have both lenses and microphones covered before starting.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.question_text: How do passenger limits, interpreter rules, and recording bans shape the cabin once your drive begins?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.teaching_text: Clearing extra passengers and disabling dashcams ahead of time prevents awkward delays right at the starting curb.

sec03-card-sec03-F32.question_text: Why does DMV prohibit automated parallel parking, lane departure helpers, and adaptive cruise control on drive day?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.teaching_text: Examiners score your own steering, spacing, and parking skill rather than software taking over pedals or wheels.

sec03-card-sec03-F33.question_text: Are backup cameras and blind-spot monitors allowed on the drive evaluation, and what must you still perform?
sec03-card-sec03-F33.teaching_text: Staring only at your center screen while reversing drops points fast if you skip physical mirror and shoulder checks.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.question_text: What principle separates prohibited vehicle assistance features from permitted safety monitors during your drive?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.teaching_text: If a feature steers, brakes, or spaces the car for you, switch it off before pulling up.

sec03-card-sec03-F34.question_text: Which two DMV web pages host sample Driving Performance Evaluation score sheets versus supplemental and area sheets?
sec03-card-sec03-F34.teaching_text: Previewing the exact grading rubric online shows every head turn, lane check, and critical error examiners mark.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: What job do traffic lanes and road markings serve, and when does a single solid yellow center line forbid passing?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Passing across a lone solid yellow is illegal whenever your travel direction has only one lane beside it.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: Which four exceptions allow crossing one set of double solid yellow lines, and what do two sets spaced two or more feet apart mean?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Treat wide-spaced double yellow pairs like a raised concrete median that blocks every turn except at open breaks.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: When may you pass across a broken yellow line, and what kind of traffic does a single solid white line separate?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Yellow always splits opposing traffic flows, whereas white paint separates lanes moving in the exact same direction.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: How do passing and turning rules step up from a single solid yellow line to one set of double yellows and twin sets two feet apart?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Each extra stripe tightens your options, moving from conditional passing limits to narrow turn exceptions and finally a median barrier.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: Where do double solid white lines appear on California roads, and when may you cross over into that lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Weaving across parallel solid white stripes into carpool lanes or across ramp borders triggers costly lane violations.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: What do standard broken white lines, wide oversized broken white lines, and painted white yield triangles each tell you?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Thick short dashes give you early warning that your lane is dropping or splitting off toward an exit.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: How do double solid white lines differ in meaning from oversized broken white dashes and white yield triangles?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Spot the shape fast so you never mistake a prohibited carpool barrier for a merging lane-drop or yield line.
sec06-card-sec06-R02.must_match_memory_hook: Solid walls, dashes warn, triangles yield

visual_sync.text_span: Solid walls, dashes warn, triangles yield

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: Which side holds California's Number one lane, and which lanes handle passing or left turns versus entering and exiting?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Highway signs and traffic reports count outward from the center divider, making lane one the fast passing side.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: What checks and speed habits make a lane change safe, and what must you do if you realize too late you are missing your turn?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Jerking the wheel across lanes for a missed turn causes side-impact crashes; keep rolling and loop back legally ahead.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: How do numbered freeway lanes organize fast passing versus ramp traffic, and how do you handle a missed exit or turn?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Planning lane moves early from left-numbered fast lanes toward right-side ramps prevents panic braking at highway speed.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: Which four vehicle groups qualify for HOV lanes during posted hours, what symbols mark them, and where may you enter?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: Motorcycles and valid clean-air decal cars share carpool access, yet everyone must still enter only at designated breaks.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: How far may you travel in a center left-turn lane, and when must a slow vehicle on a two-lane road pull into a turnout?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Cruising down a center turn lane like a passing lane causes head-on collisions, and holding up five cars requires pulling aside.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: How do access and distance rules compare across HOV lanes, center left-turn lanes, and two-lane road turnouts?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: Separate the two numbers cleanly so two hundred feet caps center-turn travel and five trailing cars triggers turnout use.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: How are California bike lanes marked, and under what three situations may a driver legally enter one within two hundred feet?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Merging cleanly into the bike lane within two hundred feet of your corner stops cyclists from getting pinched on your right.
sec06-card-sec06-F10.must_match_memory_hook: Enter bike lanes inside two hundred

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: What six bikeway styles appear on California streets, and what blind-spot and clearance rules protect cyclists and motorized bikes?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Passing closer than three feet risks clipping handlebars with your mirror or startling riders with wind blast.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: How do the two-hundred-foot bike-lane rule and the three-foot passing rule work together around bicyclists?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Stay out of dedicated bike lanes until the final two hundred feet, and always hold a three-foot side cushion.
sec06-card-sec06-R05.must_match_memory_hook: Two hundred turn, three feet pass
