sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: Where do you position your car to start a right turn, how far out do you signal, and what checks protect cyclists?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Signaling a hundred feet early and shoulder-checking right prevents right-hook collisions with riders along the curb.
sec06-card-sec06-F12.must_match_memory_hook: Right edge, signal one hundred feet

visual_sync.text_span: Right edge, signal one hundred feet

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: What is a limit line, what three-step fallback tells you where to stop if none is painted, and where do you finish a right turn?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Rolling past the thick white bar into the crosswalk forces pedestrians into live intersection lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: How does turning right on a solid red light differ from a red arrow, and what is the only legal move in a bus-only lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: Drivers routinely confuse a solid red arrow with a circular red ball, yet arrows forbid turning until green appears.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: Walk through a California right turn: signal distance, three-place stopping priority, red-ball versus red-arrow rule, and bus-lane rule?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: Combining early blinker timing, exact stop placement, and arrow discipline keeps intersection right turns ticket-free.
sec06-card-sec06-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Hundred signal, stop bar, arrow waits

visual_sync.text_span: Hundred signal, stop bar, arrow waits

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: When a dedicated right-turn lane has its own signal or channel, what can you skip and what must you still obey and yield to?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: Even when through lanes sit stopped at red, pedestrians stepping into your channel crosswalk still hold right-of-way.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.question_text: How far out do you enter a center lane and signal for a left turn, and why must your front wheels stay straight while waiting?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.teaching_text: Pre-angling your front tires left means a rear-end bump shoves your car head-on into oncoming traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.question_text: How do dedicated right-turn lanes with curb signals compare with setting up a safe left turn from the divider?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.teaching_text: Both maneuvers demand strict pedestrian yielding, while left turns add the Straight-Wheel rule until the gap opens.
sec06-card-sec06-R07.must_match_memory_hook: Curb signals right, straight wheels left

visual_sync.text_span: Curb signals right, straight wheels left

sec06-card-sec06-F17.question_text: Under what exact street combination is turning left on a red light legal in California?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.teaching_text: Turning left on red from or onto a two-way street crosses opposing lanes and is an instant red-light violation.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.question_text: What four road setups allow a signaled U-turn from the far-left lane in California?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.teaching_text: In residential neighborhoods, no approaching vehicle may be within two hundred feet unless traffic control protects you.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.question_text: At which eight locations — from railroad tracks and fire stations to business districts and one-way streets — are U-turns illegal?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.teaching_text: Fire-station driveways and business blocks mid-street are classic exam traps where flipping around is strictly prohibited.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.question_text: Pair California's one-way left-on-red rule with where U-turns are permitted versus forbidden?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.teaching_text: Check street direction before any red-light left, and verify two-hundred-foot sightlines plus business-district rules before U-turning.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.question_text: Which starting and ending lanes govern two-way lefts, standard rights, lefts from a two-way onto a multi-lane one-way, and one-way lefts?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.teaching_text: Once a one-way street carries three or more lanes, a left turn starting far-left may land in any open lane.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.question_text: How do landing lanes compare across a two-way left turn, a single-lane right turn, and a left onto a three-plus-lane one-way street?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.teaching_text: Standard turns finish tight in the nearest legal lane, while wide one-way streets unlock any safe landing lane.
sec06-card-sec06-R09.must_match_memory_hook: Hug center, hug curb, open three-lane

visual_sync.text_span: Hug center, hug curb, open three-lane

sec06-card-sec06-F21.question_text: How do left and right turns work from a one-way onto a one-way, and who yields at a T-intersection?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.teaching_text: Drivers on the terminating road at a T-intersection must always yield to cross traffic flowing along the through street.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.question_text: How should you transition off the gas to brake smoothly, and how much space do you leave behind a stopped car ahead?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.teaching_text: Stopping far enough back to see the car ahead's rear tires touch pavement gives you steering room if they stall.
sec06-card-sec06-F22.must_match_memory_hook: Coast, press gently, see rear tires

visual_sync.text_span: Coast, press gently, see rear tires

sec06-card-sec06-R10.question_text: Connect one-way-to-one-way corner starts, T-intersection right-of-way, and rear-wheel stopping space?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.teaching_text: Clean corner positioning and a visible tire cushion ahead prevent fender-benders in tight city traffic.
sec06-card-sec06-R10.must_match_memory_hook: Corner edges, T yields, tire gap

sec06-card-sec06-F23.question_text: Who yields when merging onto a freeway, what speed and following gap do you aim for, and how do you cross multiple lanes?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.teaching_text: Stopping on an acceleration ramp invites high-speed rear-end crashes and leaves zero momentum to blend into traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.question_text: How many seconds — roughly four hundred feet — ahead should you signal in the exit lane before leaving a freeway?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.teaching_text: Moving over one lane at a time and signaling five full seconds early keeps fast-moving drivers behind you from slamming brakes.
sec06-card-sec06-F24.must_match_memory_hook: Signal five seconds, four hundred feet

visual_sync.text_span: Signal five seconds, four hundred feet

sec06-card-sec06-R11.question_text: How does the three-second freeway rule when merging contrast with the five-second rule when exiting?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.teaching_text: Pair three seconds with your following cushion after merging and five seconds with your early blinker before exiting.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.question_text: How much clear distance do you need to enter city traffic versus highway traffic, and when should you hold off signaling right?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.teaching_text: Flipping a right blinker before passing a driveway tricks waiting drivers into pulling straight out across your bumper.
sec06-card-sec06-F25.must_match_memory_hook: Half block town, full block highway

visual_sync.text_span: Half block town, full block highway

sec06-card-sec06-F26.question_text: How far ahead must hills or curves be clear to pass, and within what distance of intersections, bridges, tunnels, or tracks is passing banned?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.teaching_text: Oncoming cars close head-on gaps twice as fast as you expect, making blind crests and hundred-foot approaches deadly.

sec06-card-sec06-R12.question_text: Compare the city and highway entry gaps with the clear-sight and hundred-foot ban distances for passing?
sec06-card-sec06-R12.teaching_text: Lock in one-fifty and three hundred feet for pulling out, then step up to a third of a mile for passing.
sec06-card-sec06-R12.must_match_memory_hook: Blocks to enter, third-mile to pass

visual_sync.text_span: Blocks to enter, third-mile to pass

sec06-card-sec06-F27.question_text: When is passing on the right legal, what shoulder move is always illegal, and what must you do while another car passes you?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.teaching_text: Speeding up when someone tries to overtake traps them in oncoming lanes, and driving onto unpaved shoulders to pass is illegal.

sec06-card-sec06-R13.question_text: What five-step sequence completes a pass, which three setups allow right-side passing, and how does the passed driver behave?
sec06-card-sec06-R13.teaching_text: Wait until you see the overtaken car in your rearview mirror with reentry room before signaling back over.
sec06-card-sec06-R13.must_match_memory_hook: Signal out and back, hold steady

sec06-card-sec06-F28.question_text: How much longer than your car should a parallel spot be, and what offset, angle, and curb distance finish the maneuver?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.teaching_text: Opening your street-side door without checking mirrors and blind spots invites passing traffic or cyclists to clip it.
sec06-card-sec06-F28.must_match_memory_hook: Three extra, forty-five angle, eighteen curb

visual_sync.text_span: Three extra, forty-five angle, eighteen curb

sec06-card-sec06-R14.question_text: What four key numbers guide space length, pull-up gap, backing angle, and final curb distance when parallel parking?
sec06-card-sec06-R14.teaching_text: Finishing more than eighteen inches off the curb fails road-test parallel parking and sticks your fender into traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.question_text: On the California drive test, how do you signal, check, and position your car when backing straight along a curb?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.teaching_text: Keep your head and eyes turned over your right shoulder while reversing slowly rather than staring solely at mirrors.
sec06-card-sec06-F29.must_match_memory_hook: Three car lengths within three feet

visual_sync.text_span: Three car lengths within three feet

sec06-card-sec06-F30.question_text: Which way must your front wheels point when parked downhill, uphill with a curb, and on any hill with no curb?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.teaching_text: Uphill next to a curb is the lone time wheels angle toward the street center so the curb catches rollbacks.
sec06-card-sec06-F30.must_match_memory_hook: Uphill curb away, all others right

sec06-card-sec06-R15.question_text: Pair the two threes of straight-line backing with the three front-wheel rules for parking on hills?
sec06-card-sec06-R15.teaching_text: Always engage your parking brake and shift into park or gear so gravity never relies on tires alone.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.question_text: What parking or stopping rules match white, green, yellow, red, and blue painted curbs in California?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.teaching_text: Noncommercial drivers using a yellow loading zone must normally stay with the car and move once loading finishes.
sec06-card-sec06-F31.must_match_memory_hook: White brief, green timed, yellow load

sec06-card-sec06-F32.question_text: What clearance distances apply around curb ramps, fire hydrants or stations, and crosswalks — and where else is parking always illegal?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.teaching_text: Blocking crosshatched access aisles beside blue stalls traps wheelchair lifts even if you hold a placard yourself.

visual_sync.text_span: Three ramp, fifteen hydrant, twenty crosswalk

sec06-card-sec06-R16.question_text: Review all five California curb colors: who may stop at red, who stays with the vehicle at yellow, and what unlocks blue?
sec06-card-sec06-R16.teaching_text: Even idling for thirty seconds at a red curb outside a bus by a non-bus driver earns a citation.
sec06-card-sec06-R16.must_match_memory_hook: Red buses only, blue needs placard

visual_sync.text_span: Red buses only, blue needs placard

sec06-card-sec06-F33.question_text: When is freeway or wrong-side parking legal, how long before a freeway car can be towed, and what habits save fuel?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.teaching_text: Park completely beyond the solid edge line with doors locked during a breakdown, because disabled freeway cars tow after four hours.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.question_text: When an officer flashes lights behind you, how do you pull over, set up inside the cabin, and learn the reason for the stop?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.teaching_text: Officers must state the reason for stopping you before asking questions unless an immediate threat to safety exists.
sec06-card-sec06-F34.must_match_memory_hook: Right shoulder, window down, hands visible

sec06-card-sec06-R17.question_text: How do freeway emergency parking rules and the opening moves of a law-enforcement traffic stop fit together?
sec06-card-sec06-R17.teaching_text: Even if you start in the far-left carpool lane, signal and work safely across to the right-hand shoulder.
sec06-card-sec06-R17.must_match_memory_hook: Off pavement, right shoulder, visible hands

visual_sync.text_span: Off pavement, right shoulder, visible hands

sec06-card-sec06-F35.question_text: During a stop, how should you handle search requests, required driving papers, passenger ID, exit orders, and immigration questions?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.teaching_text: You can say clearly that you do not consent to a search, yet physically resisting an officer is never lawful.
sec06-card-sec06-F35.must_match_memory_hook: Show three papers, decline searches calmly

sec06-card-sec06-R18.question_text: Which commands and documents are mandatory during a traffic stop, and which requests may you verbally decline?
sec06-card-sec06-R18.teaching_text: Refusing to show license, registration, and insurance can trigger a limited document search, whereas immigration inquiries wait for federal agents.
sec06-card-sec06-R18.must_match_memory_hook: Obey seat orders, hand over papers

sec06-card-sec06-F36.question_text: When is recording officers in public protected, what if your phone is hidden in a pocket, and when does your phone stay locked?
sec06-card-sec06-F36.teaching_text: Ask before reaching into a glovebox or jacket for a phone so an officer never mistakes it for a weapon.
sec06-card-sec06-F36.must_match_memory_hook: Announce before reaching, phones stay locked

visual_sync.text_span: Announce before reaching, phones stay locked

sec06-card-sec06-F37.question_text: Where do you file a misconduct complaint after a traffic stop, and what anti-retaliation and anti-bias protections cover you?
sec06-card-sec06-F37.teaching_text: Save disputes for the employing agency afterward rather than arguing roadside; state law requires investigation free of bias or retaliation.

sec06-card-sec06-R19.question_text: Summarize your California protections on recording officers, keeping phones locked, objecting verbally, and filing complaints?
sec06-card-sec06-R19.teaching_text: Keeping objections calm on scene and filing through the officer's agency protects both your safety and your legal record.
sec06-card-sec06-R19.must_match_memory_hook: Record openly, stay verbal, report later

visual_sync.text_span: Record openly, stay verbal, report later

sec07-card-sec07-F01.question_text: What must you do at a solid red light, a red arrow, and a flashing red light in California?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.teaching_text: Watch the California red-arrow trap: turning against a red arrow is always illegal, even after a full stop.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: How do your turning and proceeding options differ across a solid red ball, a red arrow, and a flashing red signal?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: Drivers visiting from other states often roll right on a red arrow and draw an immediate intersection ticket.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.question_text: What does a solid yellow light warn you to do, and how should you handle a yellow arrow?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.teaching_text: Protected turn time ends on a yellow arrow, so oncoming lanes may surge forward seconds later.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: What actions apply to flashing yellow lights, flashing yellow arrows, solid green, green arrows, and completely blacked-out traffic signals?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: During a power outage, blowing straight through a dark signal causes T-bone crashes because every approach must stop.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: How do flashing yellow lights, unprotected flashing arrows, protected green arrows, green exit-room checks, and dark signals compare?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Entering on green without space on the far side leaves your tail blocking cross traffic once the phase flips.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: What do WALK, steady or flashing DON'T WALK, countdown timers, diagonal crossing phases, and audible walk cues each mean?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: Even when a flashing hand tells curb walkers to wait, turning drivers must yield to anyone already mid-crosswalk.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: Where must you halt for a STOP sign, and what action does a red YIELD sign demand?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Stopping past the painted crosswalk or limit line forces walkers out into live traffic lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.question_text: How does steady DON'T WALK differ from flashing DON'T WALK, and how does a STOP sign differ from a YIELD sign?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.teaching_text: Exam questions pair flashing pedestrian hands with yield triangles to test when motion may continue versus halt.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: Which maneuvers do red-and-white regulatory signs forbid, and what standing rules or notices appear on white signs?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: Spotting a red slash or red-and-white panel tells you immediately that a turn or U-turn is banned.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: How does California's regulatory sign color code split prohibited maneuvers from standing roadway rules?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: Separating red prohibition signs from plain white standing rules lets you scan busy city poles in half a second.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: Which upcoming road conditions, lane changes, intersections, and traffic controls do yellow warning signs preview?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: Stop-ahead and signal-ahead yellow signs prevent rear-end skids around blind bends or hill crests.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.question_text: Do yellow diamond signs issue legal bans and stop orders, or preview upcoming conditions?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.teaching_text: Treat yellow diamonds as early heads-up alerts so upcoming curves, merges, or hidden stop signs never catch you speeding.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: How must you react to DO NOT ENTER, WRONG WAY, and red pavement reflectors, and what do circles, X-signs, pentagons, diamonds, and rectangles mean?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.teaching_text: Glowing red reflectors shining back from lane markers at night scream that you entered a ramp backward.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.question_text: How do DO NOT ENTER, WRONG WAY, and red night reflectors team up, and which meanings match circles, pentagons, diamonds, and rectangles?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.teaching_text: Pulling safely to the edge and backing out of a wrong-way entry immediately prevents fatal head-on freeway collisions.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.question_text: Who holds priority based on arrival at an intersection, why shouldn't you assume it, and how must you treat unsigned crossings and pedestrians?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.teaching_text: Giving up technical priority when an impatient driver barges through beats winning an argument from a tow truck.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.question_text: How does California settle simultaneous arrivals, all-way stops, T-intersections, left or right turns, and entering a backed-up intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.teaching_text: California's anti-gridlock rule tickets drivers who roll into an intersection on green without clear room to exit.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.question_text: When does the yield-to-the-right rule apply versus first arrival, and how do all-way stops, T-junctions, and turns divide priority?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.teaching_text: Watch the exam trap: yielding right fires only when two vehicles arrive at the exact same moment.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.question_text: Which direction, speed, yielding, signaling, missed-exit, and multi-lane rules govern driving through a roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.teaching_text: Stopping inside the circle or cutting across lanes for a missed exit causes instant side-swipes; loop around again instead.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.question_text: How do you enter, circulate, and choose lanes for right turns versus straight travel in a multi-lane roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.teaching_text: Crossing lane lines mid-circle clips adjacent cars, so hold whichever entry lane you picked all the way out.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.question_text: Who legally counts as a pedestrian in California, and what passing, eye-contact, and limit-line duties bind drivers at crosswalks?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: Whipping around a car stopped at a crosswalk is a deadly trap because that vehicle hides someone stepping across.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.question_text: Do skaters and wheelchair users follow pedestrian rules, how does eye contact help, and how do unmarked crosswalks compare with painted ones?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.teaching_text: Every street corner intersection creates a legal crosswalk whether or not white stripes are painted on the asphalt.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: How do you handle a blind pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, and which driver reverses on a narrow steep grade?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: Backing a vehicle uphill on a narrow mountain pass risks losing control, so the downhill driver must reverse.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: How can you tell you're in a truck's No Zone, and how far do cars versus loaded big rigs take to stop at fifty-five?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: Loaded semis need a hundred extra feet past passenger cars at fifty-five, turning cut-ins into rear-end crushes.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.question_text: What release cue applies to blind pedestrians, who yields on mountain grades, and what rule reveals truck blind spots?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.teaching_text: Honking at a blind walker confuses audible orientation; wait quietly until they pull the cane back and step aside.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.question_text: Which lanes do big rigs use on wide divided roads, how do you avoid wide-turn traps, and how do you treat safety zones and stopped transit?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.teaching_text: Trucks swing left before turning right, so squeezing along their right curb gets your car crushed against the corner.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.question_text: How do truck turn signals, rightmost-lane rules, pedestrian safety zones, and the stopped-transit passing cap work together?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.teaching_text: Raised or painted streetcar safety zones shield boarding riders, making driving across them illegal at any speed.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.question_text: Which three exceptions allow passing a streetcar or trolley on the left, and what special risks apply around light rail?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.teaching_text: Light-rail trains run quietly and can trigger signal changes ahead of normal traffic, punishing sudden left turns across tracks.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.question_text: What following gap, lane space, passing rule, and parked-car check protect motorcyclists in California?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.teaching_text: Flinging a parked car door open into traffic without checking mirrors causes devastating motorcycle dooring crashes.

sec07-card-sec07-R12.question_text: How do California's streetcar left-pass ban and light-rail signal preemption pair with motorcycle lane and gap rules?
sec07-card-sec07-R12.teaching_text: A motorcycle's narrow profile fools depth perception into thinking it shares half a lane or sits farther back.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.question_text: How must you respond to approaching sirens, parked flashers, intersection arrivals, officer commands, and trailing an emergency vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.teaching_text: If sirens catch you mid-intersection, clear through the crossing first before pulling right and stopping.

sec07-card-sec07-R13.question_text: How does pulling over for sirens differ from passing stationary flashers, and what rules cover intersections, officers, and trailing distance?
sec07-card-sec07-R13.teaching_text: Watch California's trailing number: stay outside three hundred feet behind active emergency rigs with zero grace zone.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.question_text: What speed cap and road ban govern neighborhood electric vehicles, how must you pass horses, and what road rights do cyclists hold?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.teaching_text: Revving engines or honking near horseback riders can spook animals straight into moving lanes, making scaring them illegal.

sec07-card-sec07-R14.question_text: How do NEV speed and road limits, horse anti-scaring laws, and cyclist freeway or hazard privileges connect?
sec07-card-sec07-R14.teaching_text: Cyclists may legally ride certain rural freeway shoulders when no alternate local road exists.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.question_text: Which riding rules and helmet age cutoff apply to cyclists, and what night lamp and reflector distances does California require?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.teaching_text: Exam questions swap those two night visibility distances: three hundred feet white up front, five hundred feet red behind.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.question_text: In which six situations may a slower bicyclist legally leave the right edge of the roadway?

sec07-card-sec07-R15.question_text: How do youth helmet rules and night reflectors pair with the six reasons a slow cyclist can leave the right edge?
sec07-card-sec07-R15.teaching_text: On a multilane one-way street, cyclists can ride along the far-left edge to set up left turns cleanly.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.question_text: How should you pass a cyclist, and how do you use a bike lane before making a right turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.teaching_text: Turning right across a bike lane from an inner car lane causes right-hook crashes; merge into the dashed lane within two hundred feet.

sec07-card-sec07-R16.question_text: What three-step priority governs passing a cyclist, and what window governs merging into a bike lane for a right turn?
sec07-card-sec07-R16.teaching_text: If oncoming cars block both a lane change and a three-foot buffer, slow down and wait behind the rider.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.question_text: How must you drive through cones and flaggers, what fines or jail apply in work zones, and how do you treat amber-lit trucks?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.teaching_text: California's Move Over law covers Caltrans and tow vehicles flashing amber lights, not just police and fire units.

sec07-card-sec07-R17.question_text: How do early merges, thousand-dollar doubled fines, worker assault jail terms, and amber-light move-overs combine in work zones?
sec07-card-sec07-R17.teaching_text: Waiting until the last cone to shove in triggers chain-reaction braking right beside exposed highway crews.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.question_text: Which placarded rigs stop before railroad tracks, how do you adjust in bad weather, and which lanes bind tow rigs and three-axle trucks?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.teaching_text: Tailgating a fuel tanker toward railroad tracks invites a rear-end hit because hazmat haulers must stop before crossing.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.question_text: What speed limits apply within five hundred feet of children outside a school, and what does a flashing yellow school light mean?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.teaching_text: Watch the trigger condition: California's twenty-five school-zone cap applies when children are outside or crossing within five hundred feet.

sec07-card-sec07-R18.question_text: How do hazmat rail stops, weather speed adjustments, heavy-truck lane limits, and school-zone caps fit together?
sec07-card-sec07-R18.teaching_text: Three-axle trucks and vehicles towing trailers stay in the far-right lane or the designated passing lane next to it.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.question_text: When must both directions stop for a red-flashing school bus, what penalty hits violators, and when is oncoming traffic exempt?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.teaching_text: Blowing past flashing red bus lights risks up to a thousand-dollar fine and losing your license for a year.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.question_text: When does California's fifteen-mile-per-hour speed limit apply at intersections, alleys, and railroad crossings, and where do rail warnings stop you?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.teaching_text: Memorize the sight-distance numbers: fifteen applies within a hundred feet of blind corners or rails hidden inside four hundred feet.

sec07-card-sec07-R19.question_text: How do school-bus stop rules and divided-road exemptions pair with California's three fifteen-mile-per-hour zones?
sec07-card-sec07-R19.teaching_text: Never duck around lowered railroad gates or creep closer than fifteen feet from the nearest rail while red lights flash.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.question_text: What train-awareness and exit-space rules apply on railroad tracks, and what default speed limit covers business and residential districts?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.teaching_text: Stopping in bumper-to-bumper traffic before your rear bumper clears the tracks leaves nowhere to go if gates drop.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.question_text: What does California ban regarding smoking with minors, animal dumping, fender or rear cargo overhangs, loose riders, driver video, and flaming litter?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.teaching_text: Watch those cargo numbers: zero projection past left fenders, six inches max right, and red flags or lights past four feet rear.

sec07-card-sec07-R20.question_text: How do rail exit-space rules, twenty-five district caps, and California's smoking, dumping, and cargo-overhang prohibitions group together?
sec07-card-sec07-R20.teaching_text: Night cargo overhanging four feet behind your bumper needs two red lights visible instead of a daytime twelve-inch red square.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.question_text: What corner square sizes are allowed on windshields, and what rules govern marked funeral processions and license plates?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.teaching_text: Tinted plate covers or altered frames draw citations, and cutting between headlight-lit funeral cars breaks procession priority.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.question_text: What prison, jail, and thirty-day vehicle impound penalties follow fleeing police, pursuit injuries or deaths, unlicensed driving, and speed contests?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.teaching_text: Lending or driving a car unlicensed triggers a thirty-day impound, while police chases causing death jump to ten-year prison sentences.

sec07-card-sec07-R21.question_text: How do measured corner windshield zones, funeral priorities, clean plates, and escalating police-evasion penalties line up?
sec07-card-sec07-R21.teaching_text: Exam questions contrast the five-inch lower left driver corner against the seven-inch lower right passenger corner for mounts.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.question_text: What happens when you miss court, how long stay convictions, which point totals trigger negligent status, and how often can traffic school mask a point?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.teaching_text: Adult negligent-operator thresholds step up by two points per year across one-year, two-year, and three-year rolling windows.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.question_text: What actions follow negligent point overload, which two offenses force revocation, and what proof is required to relicense?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.teaching_text: Hit-and-run and injury-causing reckless driving skip mild warnings and force license revocation, followed by financial-responsibility filings to return.

sec07-card-sec07-R22.question_text: How do missed court suspensions, thirty-six-month records, the four-six-eight point ladder, eighteen-month traffic school, and forced revocations connect?
sec07-card-sec07-R22.teaching_text: Out-of-state traffic convictions still post to your California record for at least thirty-six months.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.question_text: How do sanctions escalate across one, two, and three provisional at-fault events or substance convictions, and when do DMV hearing deadlines expire?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.teaching_text: Watch the dual hearing clock: ten days if handed notice in person, or fourteen days from the mailing date.

sec07-card-sec07-R23.question_text: Does turning eighteen wipe out provisional suspensions, and how do the one-two-three sanction steps pair with the ten-versus-fourteen-day hearing split?
sec07-card-sec07-R23.teaching_text: Teens often think their eighteenth birthday resets provisional restrictions, yet earned suspensions and probations run their full term.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.question_text: What defense rights and subpoena duties apply at a DMV hearing, who faces reexamination, and which three record items stay private?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.teaching_text: If DMV relies solely on paper reports at your hearing, subpoenaing the officer or witnesses falls on you.

sec07-card-sec07-R24.question_text: How do DMV hearing defense rights, driver-issued subpoenas, unsafe-driver reexaminations, and public-record privacy limits fit together?
sec07-card-sec07-R24.teaching_text: Crash history and convictions sit on public driving records, whereas medical conditions, home addresses, and Social Security numbers stay shielded.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: How does California color-code the four zones around your car, and how far ahead should you scan to avoid sudden swerves?

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: How do the four zone colors, the ten-second forward scan, and the three-second following rule work as one system?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Long eye lead times spot brake lights early while a three-second cushion absorbs sudden lane-cutters without chain-reaction hits.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Checking your rearview mirror before tapping the brakes warns you early if a distracted driver behind is closing too fast.
